the running program and drop `sh -c` wrappers. The lab gains a `work…`

title: feat(frontend): live process output and a Cron tab for cron jobs and monitors
body:
## What changes

- **Live output.** The shared gateway already sends `agent.terminal.output` for background processes. The plugin now adds each chunk to its process as soon as it arrives. Status and exits still come from polling `process.list`.
- **Cron tab.** The Background sheet (`/ps`, ⌥B) gets a third tab, after Running and All.
  - It lists every cron job of the profile through `cron.manage list`, paused jobs included.
  - Each job shows its schedule, next and last run, monitor target (URL or script), errors and prompt.
  - <kbd>P</kbd> pauses or resumes the selected job. <kbd>D</kbd> removes it after a confirm.
  - A job that this session's `cronjob_manage` call created gets a "this session" badge.
- **Dev:** `HERMES_TERN_EVENT_LOG=path` writes every gateway event as one JSON line.
- **Lab:** a `cron…` prompt makes two jobs through the `tool_call` bridge.

## What Hermes core does not offer yet

These items need a core change:
- Run a cron job now.
- Edit a cron job.
- Read a process's full log page by page.
- Write to a process's input.
- See or change a process's watchers.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 117 tests pass.
- Lab, headless Tern with the fake model: the Cron tab lists the jobs and shows the badge. Pause changes the state to paused. Remove asks first, then the job is gone.

title: feat: link_pull_request and a Pull requests sheet read from GitHub
body:
## What changes

**Agent tools (Python, plugin only).** These follow T3 Code's tools:
- The plugin registers `link_pull_request`, `unlink_pull_request` and `list_pull_requests` (toolset `hermes-tern`).
- It also registers one system prompt section (`register_system_prompt_section`). The section tells the agent to link every PR it opens or works on, including each stack layer. It is cache-safe: Hermes freezes it once per new session.
- Links live in `$HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-tern/pull-requests.json`, under the conversation's root session.
  - Compression gives a conversation a new session id, so the file also records an alias per lineage id.
- No GitHub call happens in the tool. A link is only the host, repository and number from the URL.

**Frontend.**
- **Links:**
  - During a live turn, it reads the list from each link tool result.
  - On resume or switch, it reads the stored links. It walks `state.db`'s `parent_session_id` chain, so links made before a compression still show.
- **GitHub data:**
  - It reads each PR with GraphQL, using `GH_TOKEN` or else `gh auth token`.
  - All PRs on one host go in one batched query.
  - It polls every 60 s while a PR is open, and every 30 s while checks run.
  - Comments and files are read only when their tab shows.
- **UI:** a PR pill above the composer (`#22 · checks passing`). The pill, `/prs` and ⌥P open the **Pull requests** sheet, which has four tabs:
  - **PRs**: state, checks, review, mergeability, changes, reviewers, labels and description.
  - **Checks**: failures first, with status, time and the log link.
  - **Activity**: comments, reviews, review threads with replies, and commits.
  - **Files**: each file's diff below the list.
- **Actions:**
  - Merge (repo's preferred method, asks first).
  - Close (asks first) and reopen.
  - Ready for review.
  - Update branch.
  - Re-run failed jobs (Actions runs from the failed checks).
  - Open on GitHub, copy URL, refresh.

## Not in this PR

- Branch matching: PRs of the session's branch or worktree that the agent did not link.
- GitHub stacks.
- The sidebar.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 127 tests pass.
- `pytest tests`: 4 Python tests pass.
- Lab (headless Tern, fake model): a `pr` prompt calls `link_pull_request` for #22 through the `tool_call` bridge. The pill shows `#22 · merged`. The sheet shows the PR, its activity and its 10 files with diffs.

title: feat(frontend): the PR of the session's branch, and its GitHub stack's layers
body:
## What changes

**The PR of the session's branch.** This follows T3 Code's `lookupBranchPullRequest`:
- It reads the checkout's branch and its upstream, then finds the GitHub repository of that remote.
- It picks the newest **open** PR with that head, else the newest PR.
- It skips the default branch. It also skips a fork's branch that has the same name.
- It works for a worktree session, because the worktree is the session's `cwd`.
- It runs on adopt, when the `cwd` changes, and after each turn. A result is trusted for 60 s when a PR was found, and for 5 min when none was.

**GitHub stacks.**
- Stack membership comes from the GraphQL `stack` field (github.com only).
- The layers come from REST `GET /repos/{repo}/stacks?pull_request=N`.
- Layers that nobody linked join the list.

**Sheet.**
- The PRs tab groups a stack's layers under a "Stack on main" header, top layer first.
- The branch's PR gets a "this branch" badge.
- The overview lists the stack's layers and says why each PR shows: linked, this branch, or stack.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 130 tests pass. New tests cover remote URL parsing, `/stacks` decoding, and a store with a linked PR, a branch PR and a stack sibling.
- Lab: a worktree on `feat/pull-requests` shows `#23 · merged` in the pill, and the agent linked nothing.
- I could not test stacks live, because I have no real stacked PR. The unit test covers them.

title: feat(frontend): a session sidebar in Tern's aside, and a Changes sheet
body:
## What changes

- **Sidebar** (⌥S, `/sidebar`). A `prefs` node in the `layer`, which Tern docks at the pane's right edge (feature `aside`, fixed 440 px). The chat narrows beside it and keeps the keys. It shows:
  - **Branch**: the name, and how far it is ahead of or behind its upstream. A button copies the name.
  - **Pull requests**: the session's PRs (linked, branch, stack), with state and checks. **Open** goes to the PR in the Pull requests sheet.
  - **Changes**: the changed files, with status and +/− lines. **Diff** opens the Changes sheet on that file.
  - It reads git every 5 s while open, after tools that change files, and after each turn.
  - Our stylesheet hides the prefs sheet's settings parts: search, page strip, page heading and brand mark.
- **Changes sheet** (`/changes`): every changed file against HEAD, staged or not, untracked files included, with the diff below the list.
- **Git state** is read as T3 Code reads it: `git status --porcelain=2 --branch`, then `git diff --numstat -M HEAD`.
- A Tern without `aside` gets a notice that says `/changes` and `/prs` still work.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 132 tests pass. New tests cover porcelain v2 parsing and numstat with renames and new files.
- Lab (headless Tern): ⌥S docks the sidebar beside a narrowed chat with branch `main`, PR #22 and 8 changed files. A Diff click opens the Changes sheet on `app.ts` with its diff.

title: feat(frontend): bridge calls show as the tools they ran; connectors show their app
body:
## Why

With Tool Search on, the model reaches deferred tools through `tool_call {name, arguments}`. It reaches connectors and MCP tools through `tool_call {calls: [...]}`. Hermes unwraps a resolved local call before it sends events. It keeps the wrapper in these cases:
- every connector call, even a single one;
- a call that it refused;
- stored history.

So these calls showed as "Tool call", with a JSON `results` blob.

## What changes

- **Unpacking** (`src/bridge.ts`, live and on resume):
  - One call shows as the tool it ran.
  - A batch keeps its entries. Each entry gets its own outcome from the `results` list.
  - A single connector call takes its entry's `response` or `error` as its own result.
- **Connectors and MCP tools** are named by app and action, as Hermes' `tool_labels.py` does: `Linear · create issue`.
  - Rows get a plug icon, with the app name in the primary text color.
  - Cards get the app as title, a `connector` or `MCP` badge, the arguments as facts, and the answer or error.
  - A batch card lists each entry with ✓ or ✗.
  - Work groups count connector calls by app ("Used Linear 2 times", "Used Linear and Slack"), and rank them with commands and edits.
- **Tool search:** `tool_search` and `tool_describe` read "Searched tools for …" and "Read how to call …". Groups sum them as "Looked up tools".

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 137 tests pass. New tests cover names, unwrap, live settle of a single call and a batch, resume, and summaries.
- Lab: a `connector` prompt sends a tool search, a Linear + Slack batch and a single Linear call. The lab has no connectors, so each entry fails. The group reads "Looked up tools and used Linear and Slack". The batch row reads "Linear · create issue, Slack · send message", and each entry shows its error.

title: fix(frontend): live steps read as running; open groups hang from their summary
body:
## Feedback addressed

1. **"Ran sed" did not show that it was running.** Two changes copy t3code here:
   - **Present tense while live.** t3code's `liveActivityToolStatus` keeps the newest step "in progress" while the turn still works. So the live line reads "Running sed", "Reading a.ts" or "Searching tools for …", until the next step or the answer replaces it.
   - **Shine.** The live line uses t3code's `live-tool-shine` effect: a band of the primary text colour sweeps across the muted words every 2.2 s. It is a light band in the dark theme and a dark band in the light theme. Tern's CSS engine rejects layer lists and `rem` (the probe showed this), so the band is a stop in a gradient three times as wide. Running rows inside an open group shine the same way. The shine is off when the system asks for reduced motion.
   - **A failed newest step** stops the group's shine, and a "Thinking" row carries the turn, as in t3code.
2. **Open groups did not look different from their rows.**
   - The rows now hang from the summary on a guide line that starts below its icon.
   - The rows are one size smaller (13 px).
   - The summary has its own chevron right after its words. The chevron turns when the group opens.
3. **Names.**
   - `granola_mcp` is shown as **Granola**.
   - "Read how to call" names connectors by app and action, not by raw `connectors__…` names.
   - `skill_view` reads "Read skill …".

The "Worked for" fold stays, as you said.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 139 tests pass.
- Lab, headless Tern:
  - Four frames 250 ms apart show the band moving across "Running sleep".
  - An open "Ran 3 commands" group shows its three rows indented on the guide line. One row is open on its output.
- The full stylesheet loads through `tern ctl css` with no parse errors.

title: feat(frontend): choose the reasoning effort and save it as the default
body:
## Why

The effort pill and ⇧⇥ changed the effort only for the current session. Nothing in `hermes tern` could make an effort the default for new sessions.

## What changes

- **`/effort`** opens a picker of every level Hermes takes: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. The session's level has a check. **Save as default** (Ctrl+G) works as in the model picker. "Set and save" sends `config.set reasoning` with `scope: "global"`, which writes `agent.reasoning_effort` to config.yaml, as Hermes' `/reasoning <level> --global` does.
  - You can also type it: `/effort high` sets the level for this session; `/effort high --global` also saves it as the default.
- **Effort pill:** click and ⇧⇥ still cycle the levels. A right-click now opens a menu with **Choose effort** and **Save effort as default**.
- **Model picker:** it now has an **Effort** strip (click it, or step with Ctrl+E). When "Save as default" is on, the picker saves the effort with the model.
- Hermes' own `/reasoning` command stays with the backend.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: all tests pass.
- Lab: `/effort`, then Ctrl+G, then a pick wrote `agent: {reasoning_effort: max}` to the lab's config.yaml. The pill showed `max`, and a notice said it is now the default. The model picker shows the strip, and Ctrl+E steps it.

title: fix(frontend): send key back at the end; the tab named after the session
body:
## Fixes

- **Send key.** Tern inserts its folder chip right before the composer bar's `status` node. #29 removed that node, so the chip went to the end and the send key sat before it. An empty `status` now keeps the chip in place and the send key at the end.
- **Tab name.** The tab now shows the session's title, through OSC 2 (Tern's pane title). The title comes from:
  - `session.info` and adopt (for a resumed session);
  - `sessions.changed`. That is the only signal viewers get when `/title` or Hermes' auto-titler names the session, and the shared gateway answers `session.title` with "unknown method". So the title is read from `session.list` by the stored session id, debounced by 400 ms.
  - The status strip shows the title too.

## Checks

- `npm run check` passes.
- Lab:
  - The send key is again at the right end of the bar, after the folder chip.
  - `/title Lab title four` renamed the tab from "hermes" to "Lab title four" within 3 s.

title: feat(frontend): sessions scoped to this project, with folders, prompts and last replies
body:
## Why

The picker showed only what the shared gateway's `session.list` serves by default: the sessions it holds live. Those rows have no folder, no prompt and no activity time. So empty "Untitled session · 0 msgs" rows filled the list, and older history could not be reached at all: 27 rows against 6,787 stored sessions.

## What changes

- **Source: `state.db`, read-only.** The listing follows Hermes' own rules (`list_sessions_rich`):
  - Local sources only (`tui`, `cli`, `local`, `desktop`, `gui`, `acp`).
  - Archived and hidden sessions are left out, unless pinned.
  - Subagent runs and compression continuations fold into their root. Each chain shows its newest part's folder, branch, model, message count and last activity.
  - Empty sessions are left out, except the one open here.
  - 400 conversations load in about 210 ms.
- **Scope, as `hermes -c` scopes it.** The first tab is this project: the pane's git repo, else its folder. A session matches when its repo root is the same, or, with no root recorded, when its folder is that folder or inside it. **All folders** lists this project's sessions first. These rules come from your OpenTUI fork's picker and from the CLI's workspace key.
- **Grouping:** by last activity (Today, Yesterday, This week, This month, Earlier), with pinned sessions on top. A **running** badge marks sessions open in another pane.
- **Search** ranks the title, first prompt, folder, branch and id. It matches whole words only; scattered letters over long prompts and paths matched nearly anything.
- **Rows:** the title, else the first sentence of the first prompt. Each row also shows the branch, and in All folders the folder name.
- **Preview:** status, folder, branch, last active, started, messages, model, a short session id, then the **first prompt** and the **last reply**.
- **Keys:** Enter resumes, Tab switches the scope, Esc clears the search and then closes, ⌫ on an empty search deletes after a confirm.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 144 tests pass. The new `sessionIndex` tests cover chain folding, subagent, cron, archived and pinned sessions, the first prompt without Hermes markers, the last reply from the newest segment, the workspace rule, and labels.
- Against the real `state.db` (read-only): 400 rows in 212 ms. The newest is "Google OAuth app submission sprint", 113 messages, oauth-lab. oauth-lab matches 7 sessions.
- Lab: the project tab lists 37 sessions and All folders 76. "errands" finds the three errands sessions. Enter resumed an older session with its transcript.
- Not tested: resuming an old `tui` or `cli` row. The gateway adopts such a row on `session.resume`, and the lab has none.

title: fix(frontend): manage_connections draws its connect card: Authorize per app, Continue
body:
## Why

`manage_connections` connect did nothing usable in `hermes tern`:
- Hermes draws its connection card only where a surface answers `connection.request`. That is the desktop, and the Ink TUI on its own gateway.
- On the shared gateway nothing answers, so the tool takes its no-card path (`tools/connectors/managed.py` `_no_card_result`). It returns at once with each app's `connect_url` and a note: "Show each connect_url to the user … Ask them to tell you when they are done, then check with action 'status'."
- Our work log folded that result away, and the agent rarely repeated the links. So there was nothing to click, and the agent went on: "While you authorize those, I'll start…".

## What changes

- **Connect card.** A no-card `manage_connections` result with links gets a card like the desktop's:
  - One row per app: the app's name ("Google Drive", from the bridge's app titles), the account alias, and the state (waiting for you, connected, failed, link expired).
  - **Authorize ↗** opens that app's link in the browser.
  - **Done, continue** sends the agent "I've authorized Google Drive and Gmail. Check with manage_connections status and carry on." While a turn runs, the message waits in the queue, so you can also steer with it.
- The card stays out of the "Worked for" fold.
- **Live state.** While a link waits, the rows refresh from `connectors.list` (session owner) every 4 s, for 15 min at most. If the gateway refuses that call, the rows keep their first states.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 148 tests pass. New tests cover parsing the no-card result, status folding (connected, expired), the continue message, and the fold rule.
- The stylesheet loads in Tern with no parse errors.

title: fix: connect card follows authorizations live; links stay out of chat
body:
## Diagnosis (of #32)

1. **No state changes.** The card polled `connectors.list`. The shared gateway answers that with "unknown method" (`gateway/session_controls.py` returns -32601 for any method not in its handlers), so the poll stopped after its first call.
2. **Links leaked into chat.** The tool's no-card result tells the model "Show each connect_url to the user", and the model followed it.
3. **Spinner.** The card claimed `running` for a call that had already returned.

## Fix

**`connections.py`**, a `transform_tool_result` hook that runs inside the gateway. It acts only for a session that a `hermes tern` pane shows. The pane writes `plugin-data/hermes-tern/viewers/<sid>.json` with its pid, and a dead pid counts for nothing. For such a session the hook:
- Writes the apps, their links and their states to `plugin-data/hermes-tern/connections/<call id>.json`.
- Removes `connect_url` from the result the model sees, and replaces the note: "The user sees these apps on a connect card … Do not repeat, paraphrase or ask for the links."
- Starts a watcher thread. Every 4 s it reads the connector list through Hermes' own `ConnectorClient`, in the session's context, and writes each app's state. It stops when every app is connected or after 15 min.
  - A reconnect counts as connected only after its status changes, because the app may already be connected before the call.
- Every other surface keeps the tool's own result.

**Pane:**
- It registers as the viewer of its session on adopt, and unregisters on quit.
- While an app waits, it reads the card file every 2 s.
- **It tells the agent by itself once every app is connected** ("Google Docs, Gmail and Google Drive are connected now. Carry on."). This is how the desktop's card settles the call.
  - "Done, continue" stays, for a partial answer.
  - A resumed session's old card never sends again.
- The card head says "N of M connected". There is no spinner.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 149 tests pass. New tests cover the card file and the viewer marker.
- `pytest tests`: 7 pass. New tests check:
  - Other surfaces, dead panes and other tools keep the tool's own result.
  - The links leave the model's result.
  - The watcher sees apps connect one by one and stops.
  - A reconnect waits for its status to change.
- Lab: the gateway loads the hook, and the pane writes its viewer marker. The lab has no connector account, so the live flow is covered by the stubbed tests only.

**The gateway must restart to load the hook.**

title: feat: parity pass 2: images, queue and steer, Markdown composer, goal and loop bars, connect card
body:
## What changes

Second parity pass, built from Sid's decisions on the open findings. Seven areas, each built in its own worktree, then merged and checked in the lab Tern.

**Images**
- A pasted image shows as a card with a thumbnail, its name and size, and a ✕. The card appears at once ("Attaching…") and fills in when the upload lands.
- On macOS the paste reads the pasteboard through JXA: about 0.05–0.13 s, against about 1.2 s for Hermes' Python extractor (which stays the fallback, and the path on Linux/WSL). A Finder-copied image file attaches that file.
- A prompt of images alone sends (Enter, the Send button, the queue). The gateway gets Ink's and desktop's text for it.
- Sent prompts show their images as thumbnails. A click opens Tern's own image viewer (zoom, pan).
- `image_generate`, `vision_analyze` and browser screenshots show the image inline, outside the folds.
- Resumed prompts no longer show raw `@image:` refs, `[screenshot]` or `--- Attached Context ---` dumps.

**Composer**
- Enter while a turn runs follows `display.busy_input_mode`. In queue mode (the default) the prompt is admitted to the gateway's queue at once, and the queued row has Steer (⌥⏎) and Edit (⌥↑), like t3code. Its bubble appears when the gateway starts it. Server-queued rows show after a resume.
- Esc Esc stops a turn (one Esc does nothing); with a draft, Esc Esc clears it into history.
- Option characters (å ∫ ß π) type text again; the panel shortcuts need Alt.
- Live Markdown styles in the composer (bold, italic, code, headings, quotes, lists, task boxes, links). ⌘B / ⌘I toggle marks. A new line in a list item continues the list. Pasted text is never collapsed.
- Known limit: Tern reports no Shift or mouse selection to the app, so ⌘B / ⌘I mark the word at the caret instead of a selection.

**Status**
- Goal and loop capsules above the composer. The goal capsule shows its state, title and a turns meter. The loop capsule shows its prompt, cadence and a live countdown. A click opens a sheet with Pause/Resume, Stop and Clear.
- Goal continuations and loop runs show as reason lines ("Loop run #2 · every 2m"), not as bubbles of internal instructions.
- Fast mode: a ⚡ on the model pill, `/fast`, and a Fast toggle in the model picker for fast-capable models.
- Effort pill: session changes go through `session.mutate reasoning` on the shared gateway, with a rollback on failure. A muted default level shows. `ultra` is added, and so is the wire clamp (`ultra→max`). Levels follow the model's capabilities.
- A reconnecting line with the attempt number and a countdown.

**Connect card** (ports the desktop's rules)
- Cards are keyed by op id. A newer connect for the same app retires the older card's row ("asked again below").
- The card survives compression, because viewer markers resolve through the compression lineage.
- A reconnect or second account reaches "connected", read from the portal account list.
- Resume shows the settled state. Continue writes a claim file, so two panes never both message the agent.

**History and tools**
- Failed and interrupted turns, stored reasoning, Codex commentary and stored inline diffs survive resume.
- Old-style async-delegation headers get labels.
- Only the newest todo card of a turn shows the full checklist. Older ones become "Plan updated: ✓ step 1, → step 2" steps.

**Slash and prompts**
- Slash replies are fenced to their session.
- Names resolve through `commands.catalog` with Ink's prefix tiers (`/hea` → `/heartbeat`; `/sta` lists its matches).
- The plugin's own commands are in completion and `/help`. `/copy [n]` and `/history` are new. Ink-only commands are hidden.
- Approval and clarify sheets close only after the answer lands, and show the error and accept a retry on failure.
- Stale prompt sheets close on resume, on a session switch and on backend exit.

**Sessions**
- A stale switch no longer detaches the live view's subscription. Detaches run one at a time per session.
- Remote subagent rows end with "outcome unknown" instead of a false "Done", and read the real outcome from the completion turn.
- A subagent's `link_pull_request` stores the link under the parent conversation.
- The session picker lists a reset conversation once.

- Lab Tern (fake model, shared gateway): ⌘V image paste in under 0.6 s with a thumbnail; an image-only send; the viewer opens on a click; the Markdown styles, list continuation and ⌘B on a word work; queue then Steer lands inside the running turn; a queued prompt's bubble shows once; one Esc does nothing and Esc Esc stops the turn; the goal capsule, its sheet and the loop capsule's countdown work; the loop run shows as a reason line; `/sta` lists its matches; `/fast` explains when the model has no fast route.

## Problem

You type `/delegation-fanout if needed` while a turn runs. The gateway queues the expanded skill message behind the turn. But the plugin drew the bubble at once, under the running turn. So the skill seemed to land only when the turn ended, and the queue had no Steer or Edit for it.

title: fix: hermes -w tern runs in the worktree, and Tern follows the session's folder
body:
## Problem

`hermes -w tern` put three views out of step. The composer's folder pill and Tern's file viewer showed the repo root. The status bar showed the worktree's branch.

## Cause and fix

- **The flag was lost.** In `hermes -w tern`, argparse stores `-w` on the top-level namespace, not in the flags that the plugin passes to `hermes chat --tui`. So Hermes' TUI launcher, which makes the worktree and points the session, `HERMES_CWD` and `TERMINAL_CWD` at it, never saw the flag. The plugin now forwards `--worktree`. `hermes tern -w` already worked.
- **Tern did not know the folder.** The frontend now sends the session's cwd to Tern with OSC 7, once when it adopts a session and again when the cwd moves. Tern's file viewer, its git branch and new splits then follow the session's folder.
- **`.gitignore`:** adds `.worktrees/`, where Hermes makes the worktrees.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 449 tests pass. pytest: 19 tests pass, including the new `tests/test_launcher.py`.
- Lab Tern, `hermes -w tern`: Tern's pane folder is `.worktrees/hermes-0f0ac795` on branch `hermes/hermes-0f0ac795`. The folder pill shows `hermes-tern/hermes-0f0ac795`.

Now each compaction is a rule across the transcript.

- **While it runs:** "Compacting context" and a timer. Automatic compaction sits inside the turn it interrupts; `/compress` sits between turns.
- **When it ends:** "Context compacted · 182K → 41K tokens · 419 messages summarized · 14s". An aborted compaction or a no-op `/compress` removes its rule.
- **Resume and reload:** the gateway's history drops the handoff summary, so the rule is placed from the summary rows in the session store (read-only; the session and the sessions it continues).
- **Click the rule:** it opens the summary the agent continues from. The handoff's instructions to the model are left out.

body:

body:
The Pull requests sheet was a list with a preview below it: most of the space was empty, comments showed raw HTML, and diffs were in a proportional font. This replaces it.

## What the user sees

- **The pill drops up a tray** (click it, or ⌥P): every linked PR with its title, repository, state and age. A pick opens that PR.
- **The PR docks at the chat's right edge** (Tern's aside). The chat narrows and goes on beside it; the composer keeps the keys. × closes it. The session sidebar and the PR aside take turns in that place.
- **A header like T3 Code's:** repository and number, state, title, author and times, `gh pr checkout N` (a click copies it), base ← head, files and +/−, and the checks' state.
- **Three tabs, as on GitHub:**
  - *Conversation:* the description, then every comment, review, review thread (with replies) and run of commits, in order.
  - *Checks:* failing and running open; passed and skipped folded.
  - *Files:* each file is Tern's own edit card with its diff, as the transcript draws an edit.
- **Tabs at the top switch PRs** when there is more than one.
- `/prs` opens the newest PR, `/prs 22` opens #22. Where Tern has no aside, the PR opens in a sheet over the chat instead.

## GitHub bodies

Comment and description bodies go through the same parsers T3 Code's PR panel uses: `remark-gfm`, `rehype-raw` and `rehype-sanitize` with GitHub's schema. Then:

- `<details>` becomes a fold.
- A badge link (an image inside a link, as Greptile writes) reads as its words.
- HTML comments go; the rest of the HTML becomes the Markdown it means, which Tern's `md` draws natively (tables, task lists, alerts, mermaid).
- `#123` links to the repository's issue and `@login` to the profile. A word joiner follows the `#`, because Tern draws `#141402` as a color chip.

## Width

Tern gives a program's aside the width of its own Settings sheet (`prefs_width`), so dragging that sheet's edge resizes the PR aside too. TSP has no drag events, so the aside cannot have a grip of its own.

## Checks

- `npm run check`: 477 tests pass (new: `prs.test.ts`, for the body pipeline and the view).
- Lab (headless Tern, fake model linking NousResearch/hermes-agent#141414, alt-glitch/hermes-tern#50 and #22): the tray, the aside on each tab, switching PRs, and a dark theme.
- The theme test now reads `white-space` as a property, not the color `white`.

The bundle grows from 1.7 MB to 2.55 MB (the unified parsers).

title: feat: tern_open opens a file, a web page or a terminal beside the chat
body:
## Problem

In `hermes tern`, the agent could not use Tern well. When asked to open a terminal next to the chat, it had to search `tern ls` for its own block. Then it told the user to type `tern open …` by hand.

The cause: the agent's tools run in the profile's shared Hermes gateway, not in the chat's Tern pane. So the agent's shell has no `$TERN_PANE`, and `tern open` and `tern split` from it go beside whatever block Tern has focused, or fail.

## Change

- **Frontend:** the viewer marker (`plugin-data/hermes-tern/viewers/<session>.json`) now also records the pane's Tern variables (`TERN_PANE`, `TERN_PANE_SOCKET`, `TERN_WINDOW_KEY`, `TERN_WINDOW_SOCKET`, `TERN_DAEMON_SOCKET`).
- **New tool `tern_open`** (`tern_open.py`): it reads the marker of the session's conversation (for a subagent, the conversation that delegated it) and runs Tern's CLI with those variables:
  - `path`: `tern open --split right|down` or `--tab`. Code, Markdown, images, PDFs and 3D models (`.glb`, `.gltf`, `.stl`, `.fbx`) draw natively.
  - `url`: a Tern browser over the chat (`tern browser` `open` op).
  - `terminal` (+ `command`, `cwd`): `tern split <pane> right|down --cwd …` or `tern new tab`, then `tern run <new block> <command>`. The command goes through Hermes' `check_all_command_guards` first, the same approval as terminal commands. If there is no verdict, nothing opens.
- **Prompt section:** only for a session that a live `hermes tern` pane shows. It tells the agent to use `tern_open` and not `tern` from its shell, and to open a file itself instead of telling the user a command.
- **Tool availability:** the tool is only offered where Tern's CLI exists (`check_fn`), so it does not show on a machine without Tern.
- **Transcript:** the work log names it: "Opened helmet.glb beside the chat", "Ran npm test in a terminal below".

## Tests

- `tests/test_tern_open.py`: a fake `tern` script logs each call and its `TERN_PANE`. The tests cover files, terminals with commands, refused commands, URLs, bad arguments, the prompt gate and the viewer lookup (lineage, subagents, dead panes, markers without a pane).
- Frontend: the marker records only the set Tern variables. The step labels are covered too.

Not tested end to end in a real Tern window: the headless lab Tern has no session daemon for the CLI.

title: feat: the agent's commands run with the chat's Tern pane, so plain tern works
body:
Replaces the `tern_open` tool from #53. The agent now uses Tern's normal CLI.

## Why it broke

- In `hermes chat` or the Ink TUI, the agent runs in a process that the pane started. Its shell inherits `TERN_PANE`, so `tern open` and `tern split` act beside the chat.
- `hermes tern` attaches to the profile's shared gateway. No pane started that gateway, or a different pane did. So the agent's commands ran without the chat's pane.

## Change

- **Frontend (from #53, kept):** the viewer marker `plugin-data/hermes-tern/viewers/<session>.json` records the pane's `TERN_PANE`, `TERN_PANE_SOCKET`, `TERN_WINDOW_KEY`, `TERN_WINDOW_SOCKET` and `TERN_DAEMON_SOCKET`.
- **`tern_env.py`:** each Tern variable joins `gateway.session_context._VAR_MAP`. That is the map Hermes copies into the env of every child it spawns: terminal commands, background processes, and the commands a Python cell runs. Hermes uses the same map for `HERMES_SESSION_*`.
  - The value is resolved when the child starts, in the spawning thread, from the marker of the session bound there.
  - A compressed conversation and its subagents resolve to the conversation's marker.
  - Concurrent sessions in one gateway each get their own pane. A conversation resumed in another pane follows that pane.
  - A session that no live pane shows keeps the gateway's own values, so a gateway that a pane started behaves as before.
- **Shared bash snapshot:** the names join `BaseEnvironment._snapshot_excluded_passthrough_names`. So they stay out of the snapshot, and the snapshot's `source` cannot replace them. This is the rule `HERMES_SESSION_*` follows.
- **Removed:** the `tern_open` tool, its prompt section and its work-log label.

## Why not `pre_tool_call` or `on_session_start`

- **`pre_tool_call`:** Hermes runs these hooks in their own thread (`hermes-hook-pre_tool_call`). A value a hook binds never reaches the thread that runs the tool. The lab showed this.
- **`on_session_start`:** it is an observer. It runs once, before the pane writes its marker. It also cannot follow the conversation to another pane.

Both hooks used here are Hermes internals. A plugin API for per-session child env would replace them (noted for upstream).

## Verified in the lab

The lab gateway was started from fake pane `AAA`. Then one session ran in pane `BBB` and the next in pane `CCC`, both with the new `ternenv` lab prompt:

| | BBB session | CCC session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| terminal `env` | `TERN_PANE=BBB` | `TERN_PANE=CCC` |
| background command | `bg BBB` | `bg CCC` |
| Python cell `terminal()` | `code BBB` | `code CCC` |

`tests/test_tern_env.py` covers: the session-to-pane lookup, the masking of the pane's unset variables, lineage and subagents, dead panes, the gateway fallback, the snapshot exclusion, and `reset_session_vars`.

title: feat: background processes chart their output live, as omp's job widgets do
body:
Ports omp's job widgets (can1357/oh-my-pi 9df0457 and 5a51063, Oct 18) to Hermes' background processes, with Tern 0.9.5's new chart props and hover cards.

**What it does**
- After a background process has printed 3+ lines for 15 s, `widget_author.py` (run in Hermes' interpreter) asks the auxiliary model, task `job_widget`, for a spec: line rules plus up to four blocks (column chart with a dashed goal line, per-key bars, meter, stats, status grid, text). Samples are redacted with Hermes' redactor before they leave. The model may decline (`skip`).
- The frontend validates the spec (dry run on the samples; goals and totals must be stated by the command or output; one retry with the errors), then applies the rules to every new line itself. Drift (200 unmatched lines, stale data) re-asks; at most 3 requests per process.
- Rules compile for V8's linear-time regex engine, so no pattern can stall the chat.
- Shown on: the shells pill (figure, trend, mini chart; hover card with a tile per running process), the background terminal card (primary chart), the Background sheet (whole chart).
- `auxiliary.job_widget` in config.yaml picks the model; `"jobCharts": false` in `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-tern/settings.json` turns it off.

**Tests**
- Frontend: 499 pass (21 new: spec validation, runtime, output tap edge cases, registry flow, views).
- Python: 27 pass (3 new for `widget_author.py`).
- Lab: new `jobchart` prompt; the fake model answers the spec request. Checked the pill, hover card, card and sheet on Tern 0.9.5.

![job chart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/feat/job-charts/docs/images/job-chart.png)

title: fix(frontend): a pasted {!cmd} or leading ! never runs; only typed ones do
body:
Pasting text that quotes `{!rm -rf /}` (a security scan report) made the chat run it through `shell.exec` on send. Hermes refused that one as dangerous, so the prompt was not sent; a command not on the danger list would have run silently.

- The composer remembers pastes that hold `{!…}` or start with `!`; `take()` forgets them.
- A prompt runs only the `{!cmd}`s that are not in a paste; pasted ones go to the model as written.
- A paste that starts with `!` sends as a prompt instead of running as `!cmd`.
- A refused prompt that goes back to the composer keeps its paste marks.

Ink avoids this by folding large pastes into `[[…]]` tokens that it never interpolates.

Tests: 500 frontend tests pass (one new: a pasted `{!rm -rf /}` stays literal while a typed `{!date}` runs; a pasted `!curl … | sh` sends as a prompt).

title: feat(frontend): job charts at omp parity: the wait card, process_manage, rules kept between panes
body:
Follow-up to #55. An audit against omp's job widgets (can1357/oh-my-pi `main` at 2220e58146, v18.12.3; no other branch changes them) found three gaps for `terminal(background=true)` processes.

**Changes**
- **Wait card.** omp tiles the jobs a `wait` watches. A `process_manage` wait, poll or log (and calls under the old name `process`) now draws its process's chart tile. While the agent waits, the card stays out of the work fold. The card title names the action ("Wait for process") and shows the process's command.
- **Tool name.** Hermes renamed `process` to `process_manage`. The plugin now matches both names.
- **Rules kept between panes.** A Hermes process outlives the pane that charted it. Each process's rules (or the model's decline) are saved to `$HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-tern/charts/<id>.json`, so another pane on the session, or a resumed one, reuses them and does not ask the auxiliary model again. The plugin checks each file again on load and deletes files older than 7 days.

**Still different from omp, and out of scope (they need Hermes core)**
- omp also reads each stage of a pipeline separately (`pipe:<n>`). Here, `cmd | tail` shows only what `tail` prints.
- omp also charts subagents that name something to watch.

**Tests**
- 503 frontend tests pass. New tests cover linking process calls by id prefix and saving rules between panes.
- In the lab, the `jobchart` prompt now also waits on the bench, and the wait card shows the live tile.
- I sent one real request through the user's auxiliary model (Nous, Opus 5.5): `widget_author.py` returned a valid spec through the `respond` tool in 4.7 s.

title: fix(frontend): charts follow log files and re-ask after setup output; one-line list details
body:
A benchmark of the job charts on real background jobs, and the fixes it found.

**Benchmark** (`lab/chartbench.ts`)
- Input: 3,215 `terminal(background=true)` jobs mined read-only from the Mac's and daimon's Hermes session databases.
- Sample: 140 jobs (90 whose output reaches the screen, 50 that write a log file still on disk).
- Each job is replayed through the real chart registry, with Haiku 5.5 as the `job_widget` auxiliary model.
- The jobs and the results stay out of the repo.

| | before these fixes | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| jobs whose output reaches the screen | 28–31 / 90 charted | 34 / 90 |
| jobs that write their output to a file | ~0 / 35 | 26 / 50 |
| request errors | 0 | 0 |
| time per request (Haiku) | ~6 s | 5.6 s |

Most of the jobs that get no chart are servers, waits, code reviews and installs. The model declines them on purpose.

**Fixes**
- **Log files.** 965 of the 3,215 jobs (30%) send their output to a file, which left the chart nothing to read. The command's log files are now chart sources `file:1…` beside `out`. Accepted path forms: absolute, `~`, `$HOME` and `$TMPDIR`, or relative after a leading `cd DIR &&`.
- **Asking again.** 148 jobs start with zsh and gitstatus start-up noise, and test runs start with setup lines. The model declined such jobs on their first lines, and the plugin never asked again. A decline is now asked again once the output has doubled and grown by 5 lines. There are still at most 3 requests per process.
- **Entities.** Model text written HTML-escaped (`ACL & update`) now reads as plain text.
- **One-line rows.** Completion, session and cron rows now show a multi-line description on one line. Skill descriptions with line breaks spilled over the rows around them in the `/` completion list.

**Tests:** 508 frontend tests pass. New tests cover log-file parsing and reading, charting from a log, asking again after a decline, and entity decoding.

title: fix(frontend): job chart numbers in readable units
body:
I replayed real background jobs from the job-chart benchmark (#58) in the lab Tern, and the charts showed numbers in poor units.

- **Units:** bytes and times now scale to a readable unit. `1.8 GB` replaces `1.8G B`, and `16 min` replaces `959k ms`. The scaling knows `B`/`bytes`, `ms`, and `s`/`sec`/`seconds`.
- **Meters:** a meter shows both numbers in the total's unit, for example `1.2/1.8 GB`.
- **Large moves:** a move of 1000% or more reads as a factor. `▲ 182×` replaces `▲ 18080%`.
- **Trend arrows:** only the latest value gets a trend arrow. The arrow compares the series' first value with its last, so on a minimum or a maximum it was wrong. For example, "fastest 2.52 s ▲ 1647%".

Tests: 510 frontend tests pass. New tests cover unit scaling, ratios and factor trends.

title: docs: scripting Tern blocks from an agent; lab replays recorded jobs
chore(frontend): bun instead of npm for installs and scripts
body:
- **Lockfile:** `bun.lock` replaces `package-lock.json`. Bun migrated it with the same resolved versions.
- **Scripts:** `setup` now runs `bun install`, and `check` now runs `bun run typecheck && bun run test`. The README, the frontend README, `docs/spec.md` and the header of `lab/chartbench.ts` now give the bun commands.
- **Frontend README:** it no longer lists an `npm run build` script, which did not exist.
- **Why bun, not pnpm:** the bundle inlines Hermes' own TypeScript through the `.hermes-src` link, and those files resolve their packages from the frontend's `node_modules`. Bun puts all packages at the top of `node_modules`, as npm does. pnpm's strict layout would likely break that.

**Checks**
- A clean `bun install` takes about 3 s.
- `bun run check`: typecheck plus 510 tests, all pass.
- `bun run bundle` produces a `dist/entry.js` that is byte-identical to the npm build.

Nothing changes at runtime: the chat still runs on the Node that Hermes starts, and the committed bundle means installing the plugin needs no package manager.

title: fix: pass the catalog's admission checks, and match the official plugins' layout
body:
This prepares hermes-tern for the community plugin catalog. It compares the plugin with the plugins in `NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins` and with the catalog rules in `hermes-agent/plugin-catalog/README.md`.

## The admission blocker

`hermes plugins validate` failed **"no core override"** (rule 9). `tern_env.py` added entries to `gateway.session_context._VAR_MAP` and patched `BaseEnvironment._snapshot_excluded_passthrough_names`. Core has no public API for per-session child environment variables, so the plugin now uses a public one that fits: a **`tool_request` middleware**.

- Before each `terminal` command runs, the middleware puts `export TERN_PANE=… …;` in front of it. The values come from the marker of the Tern pane that shows the session. This covers foreground and background commands, and the ones a Python cell's `terminal()` runs.
- Subagents get the pane of the conversation that delegated them. A resumed conversation follows its new pane.
- When a pane goes away, the next command gets the gateway's own values back.
- The model's history keeps the command it wrote.
- The frontend removes the prefix everywhere a command enters it: tool start and tool completion, the process list, and the approval sheet.

Lab test: a gateway started from pane AAA, then sessions in panes BBB and CCC. Each command, background command and Python-cell command printed its own pane, no card showed the prefix, and no stored message contains it.

## Matching the official plugins

- **`plugin.yaml`:** adds `label`, `kind: standalone`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.2"` and `provides_middleware`; drops `api_version`.
- **Python scaffolding:** a `pyproject.toml` and a root `pytest.ini`. `tests/conftest.py` loads the package as `hermes_tern_plugin`, as the official plugins do. `tests/test_plugin_registration.py` checks `register()` against the manifest.
- **Chart model:** it is now a registered auxiliary task with a plugin-namespaced key, `tern_charts` (it was the unregistered `job_widget`), so it gets its own config block and a model picker entry.
- **Windows** (the official CI runs on it):
  - The PR store now locks files with `msvcrt` on Windows, because `fcntl` is POSIX-only.
  - The pane liveness check now asks Windows for the process state. Before, it used `os.kill(pid, 0)`, which ends the process on Windows.
- **Session id:** tool handlers now take the `session_id` that the dispatcher passes, instead of importing `gateway.session_context`.
- **README:** Install (with the Hermes and Tern versions), What it adds, Development (validate, pytest, bun).
- **`frontend/package.json`:** its version now matches the plugin's.

## Validation now

`hermes plugins validate` passes, both with the installed Hermes and with `hermes-agent` main (`dfe7874`). Two warnings remain, and the catalog PR will disclose both:
- **Security scan, caution:** pattern hits in string tables, such as `sudo` in a command-label table and in Hermes' own i18n strings that the bundle inlines.
- **Private imports, at three sites that have no public API:**
  - the launcher, which runs `hermes chat --tui` in the same process;
  - the managed-connector watcher;
  - the chart helper's auxiliary call, which runs as a separate process for the frontend, so `ctx.llm` is not available there.

## Tests

- Python: 32 pass.
- Frontend: 511 pass.
- The bundle is rebuilt.

title: fix: the GitHub token comes through Hermes, never from the gh CLI's login
body:
Catalog rule 11 says a plugin never reads another tool's login, for example a vendor CLI's token. The PR view fell back to `gh auth token`, so that fallback is gone.

- **Token source:** the frontend reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` or, as a second choice, `GH_TOKEN` from its environment. For GitHub Enterprise it reads `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` or `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`.
- **Why that is the Hermes route:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a credential Hermes manages. `hermes config set GITHUB_TOKEN <token>` stores it in the profile's `.env`, and Hermes loads that file into the processes it starts.
- **No token:** the PR view says which command sets one.
- **`plugin.yaml`:** declares `GITHUB_TOKEN` under `optional_env`.
- **README:** a new **Security and privacy** section (rule 13). It lists the network calls, the command prefix, the processes the plugin runs, what it reads outside its own data, and what it stores.

`hermes plugins validate` passes. Tests: Python 32 pass, frontend 511 pass.

**Migration:** run `hermes config set GITHUB_TOKEN "$(gh auth token)"` once per profile. You copy your own token into Hermes yourself; the plugin does not read `gh`.

title: feat: tell the agent what Tern draws, and ask once for a figure that will not render
body:
## What changes for the user

In `hermes tern`, the agent now knows what Tern draws in a reply, and a diagram that would not render gets fixed without the user asking.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| The agent gets the Ink TUI's hint, so it rarely draws anything | A session a Tern pane shows is told about mermaid (35 kinds), svg figures, TeX math, 3D fences, callouts, file links and `MEDIA:` lines |
| A broken ```` ```mermaid ```` shows its source in an empty frame | The plugin checks it with merman after the turn, and asks the agent once to resend it, with the error and the line |
| `![...](/path.png)` shows a chip, not a picture | A line `MEDIA:/path` (or one that is only a Markdown image of a local file) shows the file in Tern's media viewer |

![figures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/feat/tern-render-hints/docs/images/figures.png)

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant F as Frontend (Tern pane)
  participant G as Shared gateway + plugin
  participant M as Model
  F->>G: viewer marker for the session
  G->>M: first turn: prompt includes the tern_rendering section
  M-->>F: reply with figures
  F->>F: figure_check.py (merman 0.8.0 + svg rules)
  alt a figure would not render
    F->>G: one prompt: "Mermaid diagram 1, line 3: ..."
    M-->>F: the fixed figure only
  end
```

- **Prompt section** (`render_hints.py`): only for a session with a live viewer marker. The platform cannot be used: a gateway the desktop app started reads every session as `desktop`. Other sessions on the same gateway (desktop, messaging, the Ink TUI) get nothing.
- **The diagram list** in the section is the result of drawing every merman kind in a headless Tern 0.9.5 (`tern shot`) and looking at each one: 35 kinds draw, `architecture-beta` and `info` do not. There is no plugin skill: a skill would show in the skill list of every session the gateway serves, which undoes the Tern-only gate.
- **Figure check** (`figure_check.py`): merman is the engine Tern draws with (Tern bundles merman-render 0.8.0). It is not a plugin dependency, because its wheels cover only macOS arm64, Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.35+) and Windows, and a missing wheel would fail Hermes' whole dependency sync. The script runs itself through Hermes' `uv` with `merman==0.8.0` instead: about 1.3 s on the first run, 0.1 s cached. svg figures are checked against Tern's rules: an `<svg>` root with a `viewBox`, no scripts, `foreignObject`, event handlers or external `href`.
- **One ask per user prompt**, claimed by one pane when several show the session.

## Known limits

- `architecture-beta` passes merman's parser but Tern does not draw it. The prompt and skill steer away from it, and the check flags it.
- merman 0.8.0 from PyPI can still disagree with Tern's vendored copy in edge cases.
- The fix arrives as a second turn. Core has no hook to keep a text-only turn going; NousResearch/hermes-agent#101910 tracks one, and a `pre_finish` hook is drafted.
- Upstream asks from this work are filed under NousResearch/hermes-agent#141982 (client render capabilities: #141974).

## Checks

- `uv run --with pytest --with merman==0.8.0 pytest -q`: 35 passed
- `bun run typecheck`, `bunx vitest run`: 517 passed
- Lab, end to end in a headless Tern with the fake model (`figures` flow): the section reached the system prompt, the broken diagram triggered one fix prompt, and the fixed diagram, math, the literal `\$5`, the svg figure and the `MEDIA:` image all rendered (screenshot above)
- `hermes plugins validate .`: same result as `main` (the security scan flags the bundled frontend, as before)



_Rebased onto main after #67: the after-turn figure check moved from `app.ts` into `app/actions.ts` (`checkFigures`), called from `turn/fanout.ts`; `frontend/dist/` is no longer in this PR (#78)._

title: fix(frontend): approval sheet: one button per answer, and the whole command
body:
The approval sheet was hard to read and slow to answer:

- Its four answers were radio rows with a description under each, plus a **Choose** button. Answering took two steps, and **Deny** appeared twice: once in the list and once as a button.
- A long command stayed on one line and ran off the edge of the sheet, so the part that matters could be hidden.

Now:

- **One button per answer:** Deny · Always allow · Allow for this session · **Allow once** (the primary button, on Enter). Each description moves to its button's tooltip.
- **The reason** ("Flagged · …", or the safety check's advice against the command) sits under the question.
- **The whole command wraps**, up to 12 lines.
- **Keys:** Enter or `y` allows once, `s` allows for the session, `a` always allows, and Esc or `n` denies. A key with Ctrl, Alt or Cmd does nothing. A choice the request does not offer, such as "always" after a smart-guard deny, has no button and no key.
- **Lab:** the fake model's `approve long` prompt sends a long chained command, to check the wrapping.

Tests: `bun run check` passes (520 tests). The new tests cover the buttons, each key, the offered choices and the wrapped command. I checked the sheet in the lab Tern with `approve` and `approve long`, and answered it with `s`.

title: ci: checks for every PR and push to main
body:
Adds `.github/workflows/checks.yml`, with two jobs. The `main` ruleset will require both of them once the repository is public.

| Job | What it runs |
| --- | --- |
| `python` | `pytest` on Python 3.11 (the plugin's `requires-python` floor), through uv |
| `frontend` | It checks out `NousResearch/hermes-agent` main as `HERMES_SRC`, then runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `typecheck`, `test` and the bundle build |

title: refactor(frontend): split app.ts, transcript.ts and the tool views into typed modules, with ratchets and golden replays
body:
The frontend grew one feature at a time into a few very large files. `app.ts` alone had 2,873 lines, including a 415-line `switch` over every gateway event. This PR splits it into small typed modules, with one folder for each concern. It makes no change you can see in the UI, except for the bug fixes listed below. > **TL;DR** > - `app.ts` (2,873 lines) → `app/` + `gateway/` + `session/` + `turn/` + `draft/`. The largest new file is 586 lines. > - Gateway events go through a typed handler table. Tool cards go through a tool registry. Session switches go through one staleness primitive (`Epoch`). > - 27 work packages (`WP00`–`WP26` in the commit subjects), then 13 commits that fix the review findings. Tests go from 520 to 874, and golden replays prove that the UI output did not change. > - Python: no change. If a card throws, the generic card draws in its place, and the pane reports it once for each tool name.
Session switches: #reading flags → Epoch tickets Before: a git read for session A that ended after you switched to B wrote A's state into B's sidebar. The `#reading` flag also dropped B's first refresh. ```diff - async refresh() { - const cwd = this.#app.info?.cwd || null - if (this.#reading) return - this.#reading = true - clearTimeout(this.#timer) - try { - this.#state = cwd ? await gitState(cwd) : undefined - this.#cwd = cwd - } finally { - this.#reading = false - if (this.#open) this.#timer = setTimeout(() => void this.refresh(), POLL_MS) - this.#app.changed() - } - } + async #refresh(ticket: Ticket) { + if (!this.#open) return + const cwd = this.#host.session.info?.cwd || null + const state = cwd ? await this.#read(cwd) : undefined + if (ticket.isCurrent()) { // stale once another session is adopted + this.#state = state + this.#cwd = cwd + } + } ``` `core/epoch.ts` has about 40 lines. `core/poller.ts` builds on it, and the sidebar, cron, agents, processes, GitHub and connect-card stores use `Poller`.

title: feat(frontend): /rewind goes back to any earlier prompt, to rewind or branch there; /undo N counts
body:
`/undo` and `/retry` only reach the newest prompt. `/undo 3` also undid just one: the count was dropped.

- **`/rewind`** opens a sheet with the session's prompts as a timeline, read from a fresh `session.resume`. Each prompt shows its reply, and the newest is picked.
- **Enter rewinds.** After a confirm in the sheet, `session.mutate` `rewind` targets the picked row. The transcript reloads, and the prompt's text goes back in the composer to edit and send, as the CLI's `/undo` does. Images the prompt carried don't come back, and the notice says so.
- **B branches.** `session.mutate` `branch`, with `through_message_id` set to the stored row before the prompt, copies the session up to that prompt. The view moves to the branch with the prompt in its composer. The original keeps its history. The first prompt has nothing before it, so there the button is off and points to `/new`.
- **Both writes check the row first.** `mutateSession` re-reads the session. If the picked row is no longer that prompt, nothing is written and a notice says so. The sheet won't open or act while a turn runs or prompts are queued.
- **`/undo N`** backs up N prompts, clamped to the oldest, the way the CLI's `undo_last` counts. A count that isn't a whole number above zero gets a usage line and sends no request.
- Session commands get a `draft()` port. It puts text in the composer ahead of any draft there, as `restore()` does.

This is plugin-only. The shared gateway already serves both operations, and `hermes_state_mutations.py` validates `target_message_id` and `through_message_id`.

Tests: `bun run check` passes (885 tests). The 11 new ones in `rewind.test.ts` cover the targets, the sheet's keys and confirm, a row that disappears between the read and the write, the branch boundary, the first prompt and `/undo N`. `pytest` passes (32 tests).

Checked in a headless `tern serve` (not a signed-in Tern window), with a real model (OpenRouter `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free`) and a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`:

- Ran three turns, then `/rewind` on the newest prompt. Its two rows went `active=0` in `state.db`, the prompt came back in the composer, and sending it ran a new turn.
- `/rewind`, then B on the second prompt. This made a child session with `parent_session_id` and `_branched_from` that holds a copy of the first exchange. A turn then ran on the branch.
- B on the first prompt did nothing.
- `/undo 2` removed the last two exchanges.
- I looked at the sheet 1280 and 960 points wide.

title: feat(frontend): /tree shows a conversation's branches, and opens one
body:
`/branch` copies the session, and `/sessions` lists every copy as a row of its own. Nothing shows which copy came from which, so after a few branches it's hard to find your way back.

- **`/tree`** draws the shown conversation's branch family as a tree. Each branch sits under the one it copied, and the open one is marked. Enter opens the picked branch in this view, as `/sessions` does. The preview shows the branch's source, its branch count, its dates and size, its first prompt and its last reply.
- **Data:** the family comes from `state.db`, read-only, the same way the session picker reads it. The shared gateway serves no lineage. A branch is a copied session whose `parent_session_id` names its source. Newer branches carry `_branched_from` in `model_config`. Older ones are known only because their parent ended `branched` before they started, which is how `hermes_state_sessions.py` reads them too.
- **Folding:** a compression continuation belongs to its conversation's root, so the open view finds its node even when it shows a later segment. Subagent runs, tool sessions and reset segments are left out.
- **Damaged lineage:** if parents form a loop, the loop is cut at its smallest id. Every member of the loop then draws the same tree.
- **Unknown cut points:** Hermes doesn't record where in its parent a branch was cut. The tree shows when each branch started and doesn't guess the message.
- A conversation with no branches gets a notice instead of a one-row sheet.

This is plugin-only. Nothing changes in Hermes, and no new RPCs are added. It's independent of #68, but the two work together: B in `/rewind` makes a branch that `/tree` then shows.

Tests: `bun run check` passes (882 tests). The 8 new ones in `sessionTree.test.ts` cover: the whole family read from any member and from a continuation; subagent and reset rows left out; a legacy branch kept; a loop cut the same way from both ends; a missing session or database; tree order and depth; and the sheet's current mark, Enter, and the no-branches notice. `pytest` passes (32 tests).

Checked in a headless `tern serve` (not a signed-in Tern window), with a real model (OpenRouter `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free`) and a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`:

- Made a conversation with a branch of a branch (`/branch` twice) and ran a turn on each.
- `/tree` from the deepest branch showed all three nested, with that branch marked.
- Enter on the root moved the view to it.
- I looked at the sheet 1280 and 960 points wide.

title: fix(frontend): every control a click works on is a native button with a name
body:
Tern focuses buttons and fields only. The pane drew its controls as clickable rows, icons and keys (`row onClick`, `icon onClick`, `actions.click`), so they worked with a pointer and nothing else:

- Tab never reached them, and Enter or Space did nothing.
- A screen reader found nameless groups. `tern ctl a11y` on `main` lists the Send key as `Image "Return"` and Help's Close as a `Group`, neither focusable, and a copy icon has no node of its own.

Now:

- **`pressable()`** (`view/ui/button.tsx`) puts a control inside an `el` button (`html.button`), named with `aria`. The button takes the click, the menu and the action. The control keeps omp's role, so it looks the same: Tern's sheets style `.sf-row[data-role='omp.btn']` and the like by kind, and Kit resets the button's own look. `styles.ts` makes the button exactly as big as the control.
- **The role moves to the button** where Tern styles a role on any kind or hides it: Send, Stop, and the working row's Stop, which Tern hides (the composer has one). A hidden control then leaves no hidden tab stop.
- **Converted:** `button()` (every sheet's action row and the PR actions), the pills and the goal and loop capsules, Send and Stop, queued Edit and Steer, copy under prompts and answers, the image chip's ✕, the PR sheet's checkout command, checks summary and file list, the PR menu rows, the connect card's Authorize and Continue, and a background card's process line.
- **The status strip's send and stop segments** get an `aria` name. A `seg` has to stay a `seg`, and each one repeats a composer button.
- **Not converted: the composer's model and effort chips.** Tern's composer finds them by role among the bar's children. At a narrow width it cuts the effort chip and draws its glyph on the model chip. With a button around either chip, that stopped at 400px. They are still named by their titles, and ⇧⇥ and `/model` reach them from the keyboard. If Tern made a clickable row focusable, these two could follow.

**Ratchet:** `a11y.test.ts` walks every frame of the golden replays, plus what they do not reach: the dock with every pill, the goal and loop line, the PR sheet, a connect card and a process line. It lists any click target that is not a named button, any nameless button, and any button inside a button. So a new control drawn as a clickable row fails it. When the button is turned back into a `div`, 6 of its 7 tests fail. The golden and tool-card snapshots change only by the wrapper and the two segment names. I checked this with a script that unwraps the buttons: the frames then match `main`, and the requests and answers are the same.

Tests: `bun run check` passes (881 tests; lint, size, strict and suppressions ok), `dist/entry.js` is rebuilt and matches a fresh build, and pytest passes (32).

Checked in headless `tern serve` on Tern 0.9.4, not in a signed-in window. The plugin ran in a scratch `HERMES_HOME` with real turns on an OpenRouter model:

- `tern ctl a11y` (tern serve capture), before → after:

  | Control | `main` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Send key | `Image "Return"`, not focusable | `Button "Send"`, focusable |
  | Help's Close | `Group "Close escape"`, not focusable | `Button "Close"`, focusable, same box |
  | Copy under an answer | no node of its own, inside an unnamed `Group` | `Button "Copy answer"`, focusable |
  | Status strip's send | unnamed `Group` | `Group "Send"` |

  Also as focusable, named buttons on this branch: Stop while a turn runs (the hidden working-row Stop is absent), Copy message, the shells pill ("1 shell running"), the process line ("Process running: open in the Background sheet"), and queued Edit and Steer.

- **Keyboard:** I focused each button through AX and pressed a key. Space on Help's Close closes the sheet. Space or Enter on Copy answer copies it, and its name turns to "Copied". Space on a queued prompt's Edit pulls the prompt into the composer. Space on Stop interrupts the turn. Tab goes from Copy message to the "Worked for" fold to Copy answer. A key pressed while a button has focus goes to that button, not the composer: Enter on Copy answer left the draft unsent.
- **Pointer:** clicks on Copy answer and Edit work as before.
- **Look:** on the same resumed session, `tern ctl dump` gives the same element boxes on `main` and here. That covers the composer bar at 1280px and 400px (the effort glyph moves onto the model chip as before), the Send key, the copy and usage icons, the process line and the pill's parts. Focus draws Tern's default ring.
- **Not run live:** the PR sheet, the connect card and the goal and loop capsules. They need a linked PR, a connector and a goal, which the scratch session did not have. The unit tests and snapshots cover them.

Thanks to Stencil (Can Bölük) for Tern's `el` button and `aria`, which made this a wrapper and not a rewrite.

title: feat(frontend): dictate into the composer with Hermes' own speech-to-text
body:
## What

Dictation in the composer. `/voice on` turns it on for the pane. After that, <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> (or `voice.record_key`) opens the microphone, and the words land in the composer at the caret. They are never sent: you read the draft and press Enter yourself.

![The capture row above the composer while the microphone is open](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/raw/72b455ab60d3860cf60bbea192efe97d261e9ea1/listening-row.png)

- **Off by default.** Until `/voice on`, no key opens the microphone, and the record key types as it did before. `/voice on` first runs Hermes' own requirements check (the one `/voice status` prints in Ink). If the microphone or the STT provider is missing, it prints the report and stays off. `/voice off` turns it off again.
- **You can always see it.** While dictation is on, a mic sits on the composer's bar. While a capture runs, a row above the editor says Listening… or Writing it down…, shows what a streaming STT provider has heard so far, and has Done and Cancel buttons. The mic turns red.
- **Cancel is easy.** <kbd>Esc</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> or Cancel throws the capture away. Ctrl+C drops the capture before it touches the draft. The record key, <kbd>Enter</kbd> or Done ends the capture and keeps the words. Enter does not send while a capture runs, and neither does Tern's own send (`sendable` is false then).
- **One undo step.** The words go in with one splice, with a space on each side where needed. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> takes them back out.

## Why it runs beside the pane

The shared gateway has no `voice.record` (it is not in `CANONICAL_RPC_METHODS`). Also, the microphone belongs to the machine the pane runs on. So recording happens in `dictation.py`, which runs in Hermes' interpreter the same way `widget_author.py` does. It calls the same code Ink's push-to-talk uses: `hermes_cli.voice.start_continuous(auto_restart=False, …)`, with `voice.silence_threshold`, `voice.silence_duration` and `voice.max_recording_seconds`, and the STT provider in `stt`. It writes JSON lines (`state`, `partial`, `text`, `error`) and reads `stop` / `cancel` on stdin. If stdin closes, it cancels, so a pane that exits releases the microphone.

The frontend side:

- `hermes/dictation.ts` starts the helper and parses the record key.
- `draft/dictation.ts` is the store. Each capture has its own identity, and lines from a cancelled capture are dropped. A new capture waits until the last helper has exited.
- `view/dictation.tsx` draws the row and the mic.
- `commands/voice.ts` handles `/voice`.

Before this change, `/voice` went to the gateway's `slash.exec`, which only sets the session's messaging voice mode.

**Record key.** If `voice.record_key` names a key, that key is used. The forms are the ones Ink accepts: one modifier and one key. One exception: Hermes' default <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> becomes <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> here, because Tern's editor uses Ctrl+B for bold on Linux and the chat never gets the key. I saw this in `tern serve`. A chord that one of the pane's own shortcuts already uses also falls back to Alt+V.

**No hold-to-talk.** `@stencil-hq/tern` 0.1.0 reports key presses but not releases, so the record key toggles.

## Tested

- `bun run check`: typecheck, 891 tests, lint, size, strict, suppressions. `dist/entry.js` was rebuilt and matches `node scripts/build.mjs`. `pytest`: 37 passed.
- New `frontend/src/__tests__/dictation.test.ts`: the line decoder, record key parsing, and the store with a fake recorder (caret placement, one undo step, Esc and stale lines, the wait for the microphone to close, errors, `/voice off`). It also covers the real `spawn` path against a stand-in helper script, and the app end to end: `/voice on` reads `config.get {key: 'full'}`, Enter ends the capture without a `prompt.submit`, and the words are sent only by the next Enter. `keys.test.ts` covers where the rule sits in the chain and Ctrl+C. If you remove the Enter guard in `submitDraft`, the app test fails.
- `tests/test_dictation.py`: the helper against a stubbed `hermes_cli.voice`. Covers stop, cancel, closed stdin, VAD stop, a busy microphone, start errors, `--check`, and the config fallbacks.
- **Headless `tern serve`** (Tern 0.9.4), with the plugin installed in a separate `HERMES_HOME`, real Hermes 0.22.2 and a real model (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free`):
  - `/voice on` passed Hermes' check.
  - Alt+V started `dictation.py` in Hermes' interpreter and opened the machine's real input. The capture above is from that run.
  - Esc released the input, and the helper exited within the next 4 s.
  - The record key followed by Enter wrote nothing (the room was silent). The pane said "Dictation heard nothing." and kept the typed draft.
  - Sending that draft ran a normal turn:

  ![The turn after a capture that heard nothing](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/raw/72b455ab60d3860cf60bbea192efe97d261e9ea1/real-turn-transcript.png)

title: fix(media): bound image downloads before buffering
body:
## Problem

`Media.#bytes()` previously used `response.arrayBuffer()` after checking `Content-Length`. A remote image without a size header (or with an incorrect smaller header) could be fully buffered before the existing 16 MiB Tern blob cap rejected it. Oversized `data:image/*;base64` URLs were also decoded before size validation.

## Change

- Stream remote image bodies under the **existing 16 MiB limit**; reject and cancel as soon as the next chunk would exceed it.
- Use `Content-Length` only for early rejection, not as proof the body fits.
- Reject oversized base64 payloads before decoding.
- Narrow untyped stream chunks before trusting their size/bytes.
- Add four tests: headerless success, declared oversized image, unknown-length overflow/cancellation, oversized data URL.
- Rebuild and commit the pinned `frontend/dist/entry.js`. No plugin API or Hermes core changes.

## Evidence

- Fork CI: [verified typecheck, 878 Vitest tests, lint, size/strict/suppression ratchets, bundle](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/actions/runs/39522394483) on source `6354261c` (generated bundle committed afterward).
- `frontend/hermes-src.lock` remains pinned to `22063fc099ec9ad8357d7f8f6e6248a0400680d3`.
- No real-host Tern E2E claim; HTTP response limits are unit tested.
- No new workflow or dependency is included in the PR.

## Prior work and provenance

The bounds/session-lifetime audit was motivated by [the downstream Hermes × Tern media implementation](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/blob/724b2aaec5981eb264f65923f72858faff27bb5b/ui-tsp/src/media-delivery.ts), adapted to this plugin's existing `Media` architecture rather than importing its code. Credit to Can Bölük / Stencil Labs for the original TSP frontend, alt-glitch for the standalone plugin, and NousResearch/Hermes contributors for the gateway.

title: fix(media): bind image previews to session and pane lifetime (stacked on #72)
body:
## Depends on #72 — review the incremental diff

This is a **stacked, draft PR** built on [#72's fork branch](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/tree/fix/media-stream-bound). Until #72 merges, the GitHub PR comparison against upstream `main` also includes its bounded-streaming patch. **Please review just [the second-slice diff](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/compare/fix/media-stream-bound...fix/media-session-lifetime).**

## Problem

The plugin's `Media.show()` fetch may resolve after `session.resume`, a session switch, or pane shutdown. It previously could still create a Tern blob, fill the previous `ToolCall.image`, cache a preview keyed only by URL, and schedule a redraw. A same-session transcript reattach also resets the tool-call objects.

## Change

- Reuse the plugin's existing `Epoch` to give media requests a generation and abort signal.
- Invalidate pending image fetches, caches and callbacks **before every transcript adoption** (new session, resume, or reattach) and when the frontend closes.
- On late resolution, reject blob upload, old tool-call mutation, cache fill and redraw; don't poison the next session's same-URL request.
- Combine epoch abort and existing 20 s network timeout.
- Regression tests for stale completion, same-URL reuse and abort propagation, plus ordered invalidation in existing lifecycle tests.
- Regenerate `frontend/dist/entry.js` against the existing pinned Hermes checkout.

## Evidence

- [Fork CI — 881 frontend tests and all typecheck, lint, size/strict/suppression and bundle steps passed](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/actions/runs/39522897016).
- Existing `frontend/hermes-src.lock` unchanged.
- No live Tern-host screenshot or end-to-end acceptance claimed.
- No temporary CI workflow remains in this proposed diff.

## Provenance

The session-owned preview invariant is adapted to this plugin from [the downstream Hermes × Tern media-delivery contract](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/blob/724b2aaec5981eb264f65923f72858faff27bb5b/ui-tsp/src/media-delivery.ts); this code uses alt-glitch's own `Media` architecture and `Epoch` utility. title: fix(frontend): a readable completion list
body:
The `/` and `@` completion list was hard to read: skill descriptions stopped after about 40 characters.

## Before → after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Place | Opens at the caret, wherever the `/` or `@` was typed | Fixed above the composer, aligned with its left edge |
| Width | Grows with its rows, at most 600px | As wide as the composer (736px, or the pane's width, if that is less) |
| Names | Monospace, at most 45% of the row | The UI font, semibold, at most 40% of the row. `@` and path rows stay monospace. |
| Descriptions | Dim (`--t3`), with a `⚡ ` before each skill's | One step brighter (`--t2`), without the `⚡` (the bulb icon already marks a skill) |
| Long descriptions | Cut off with `…` | Still cut off in the row, but a footer under the list shows the highlighted row's whole description, up to 3 lines |
| Typed-text match | Shaded box | Accent-colored letters |

## Why a footer, and not a taller highlighted row

Tern places list rows at fixed 32px steps. A highlighted row that wraps does not grow: its text spills over the next rows (I tried it in the lab). The footer is shown for the whole list while any row is too long, so the popup keeps its height as you move the highlight.

"Too long" is an estimate from character counts (`cutOff()` in `overlays/completion.tsx`), because the frontend cannot measure the rendered text. A row that only just fits can still show the footer. That does no harm.

## Changes

- `overlays/completion.tsx`:
  - the overlay anchors to the composer node (`{node: 'dock.composer', side: 'above'}`), not to the caret; `surface/host.ts` exports `COMPOSER_ID`, and `app/frame.ts` passes it;
  - each row gets a `role` (`hermes.complete.command`, `.skill` or `.path`) for the stylesheet;
  - `detailOf()` removes the `⚡`;
  - the footer is a `hermes.complete.more` text.
- `view/styles.ts`: the list's width, fonts and colors, and the footer.
- Tests:
  - the `⚡` is removed;
  - each row has its role;
  - the footer shows only while a row is too long.
- `dist/entry.js` is rebuilt.

## Checks

- typecheck, lint, the ratchets and 876 tests pass.
- Checked in the lab: `/` commands, inline `/skill` references (the list stays at the composer's left edge), and `@` mentions.

body:

Why it still hangs today: this PR was never merged. Tern `main` lists `connection.request` and `connection.update` as ignored events (`frontend/src/gateway/coverage.ts`), so the shipped bundle never draws the card. The card protocol did not change on hermes-agent `main` since this PR was opened (checked against `6b21d0564d`).
