title: refactor: the connect card is the gateway's only; remove the connections hook
body:
The plugin no longer rewrites `manage_connections` results or runs its own watcher thread. The connect card in the pane is the gateway's own card only. This removes the plugin's last imports of private Hermes modules, and 2,026 lines.

![The gateway's connect card in the pane](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31e7ca1d-1bc1-4d5d-9b4e-005c44779da3)

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why

Before the gateway sent a connect card, the plugin made one itself. A Python `transform_tool_result` hook rewrote the tool result, wrote card files under the plugin's data folder, and ran a watcher thread. The frontend drew those files.

Since #76 the pane draws the gateway's card (`connection.request`, `connection.update`, `connection.respond`).

- The old path is dead for every session a pane shows. Hermes gives each turn of a local session the card callback (`gateway/local_desktop_ui.py`, `wire`).
- The old watcher is broken on Hermes `main`. It calls `managed_client()` without the keyword `creates_guest`, which is now required, so every old card ended as `error`.

## What changes

| Area | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connections.py` | hook, watcher thread, card files, 3 shared helpers | deleted |
| Private imports | `tools.connectors.managed` | none |
| `plugin.yaml` | `provides_hooks: [transform_tool_result]` | no hooks |
| Frontend card | gateway card and file card | gateway card |
| Guards for a Hermes without `ctx.register_rpc` or `ctx.register_session_env` | 3 | none (the pane checks capabilities at connect since #97) |

The three helpers that other modules used get a proper home:

- `sessions.py` is the one module that imports `hermes_state`. It holds the conversation's compression lineage, the delegating conversation of a subagent, a session's stored row and the read-only database handle. Two identical copies of the lineage function become one.
- `plugin_data.py` holds the plugin's data folder.
- `processes.py` holds the check for a running process.

In the frontend, `dataDir` moves from `connections/cards.ts` to `config/dataDir.ts`, because the pane restore and the chart memory use it too. `AppActions.submit` loses its `draft` flag: its only `false` caller was the message the pane wrote to the agent after a file card settled.

## Behaviour that changes

A `manage_connections` result that carries links but has no gateway operation now shows as a plain tool row. Before, the pane drew a card from the plugin's file. This cannot happen for a session a pane shows, for the reason in "Why".

## Verification

- `pytest`: 86 passed. `bun run check`: 964 tests, lint and the three ratchets pass.
- `hermes plugins validate` on a fresh clone no longer prints a "private core imports" line.
- Live, against a real gateway in a headless Tern with the lab's fake model:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `install figma` | the gateway's card, with Connect, Not now, the "Connects to" line and Continue (screenshot above) |
| Not now | the card settles and the turn ends |
| A typed prompt while the card waits | the card settles as Continue and the prompt runs |
| Gateway log | no watcher line and no traceback from the plugin |
| `ternenv` | the command prints its `TERN_PANE` value (the lineage helper) |
| Kill the frontend, start it again | "Resumed the session after the pane restarted." |
| `pr <url>` | the link is stored and listed |

</details>

title: refactor(frontend): one gateway kind, and the clipboard image through hermes clipboard image
body:
The frontend no longer carries code for a second kind of gateway that it can never reach. On Linux, Windows and WSL, a pasted image is now read with `hermes clipboard image --json`. macOS keeps its fast pasteboard script.

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why

The frontend once ran against two kinds of gateway: Hermes' shared gateway, and a private one that each TUI process started for itself. Since #91 it only attaches to the shared gateway, with `hermes gateway attach --json`. Eleven files still branched on `gw.isCanonical`, and the other arm of each branch never ran.

The frontend also read a pasted image with its own `wl-paste` and `xclip` code. Hermes now ships that as a public command, which also serves Windows and WSL.

## What changes

- **Deleted arms.** Every `isCanonical` branch, and the calls that only the private gateway took: `session.close`, `session.title`, `image.attach`, `config.set` for the model and for the session effort.
- **Deleted with them.** The `cols` parameter on `session.create` and `session.resume`, `hermes/create.ts`, and the model picker's "Save as default" toggle with its Ctrl+G key. The toggle was shown only on a private gateway.
- **Queue.** A prompt sent during a running turn always goes to the gateway's queue. The pane no longer holds such a prompt itself.
- **Unused exports.** `processId`, `subagentId`, `cardKey` and `CardKey` in `core/ids.ts`.
- **Clipboard.** `hermes/clipboardImage.ts` runs `hermes clipboard image --out PATH --json` with the command the launcher hands the frontend, the same one `hermes gateway attach` uses. On macOS the JXA script runs first, and the Hermes command is the second try when the script cannot run.

| Clipboard result | What the user sees |
| --- | --- |
| exit 0, `ok: true` | the image attaches |
| `reason: no_image` | "No image on the clipboard" |
| `reason: no_tool` or `write_failed` | Hermes' own message |

## Behaviour that changes

- With no clipboard tool installed on Linux, the user now sees Hermes' message that names the missing tool. Before, the pane said "No image on the clipboard".
- Four commands typed before the first connection (`/undo`, `/retry`, `/compress`, `/branch`) now answer "No active session". Before, they went to `slash.exec` on a gateway that was not connected.

## Verification

- `pytest`: 86 passed. `bun run check`: 957 tests, lint and the three ratchets pass.
- The golden replay changes in one way: two `"cols": 100` fields leave `session.resume`.
- Live, against a real gateway in a headless Tern with the lab's fake model:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New session, `hello` | a reply |
| A prompt sent during `slow` | it runs after the first turn |
| `/title Lab title` | the title shows |
| `/model` | the picker opens with no "Save as default"; the session keeps working |
| An effort change | the next prompt gets a reply |
| `/image <path>` then a prompt | the bubble shows the image |
| `/new`, `/quit` | a second session opens; the pane exits with no error |
| `hermes clipboard image --out … --json` with an image on the clipboard | `{"ok": true, … "mime": "image/png"}`, exit 0 |
| The same with no clipboard tool on `PATH` | `reason: no_tool`, exit 3 |

</details>

title: refactor: stored sessions, compaction markers and pull-request links come from the gateway
body:
The session picker, its preview, the compaction markers and the pull-request links no longer read Hermes' `state.db` from Node. They use the gateway's `session.list` and `session.transcript`, and one plugin RPC method. One reader of `state.db` remains, the subagent pane, and the next PR removes it.

![The session picker, filled from session.list and session.transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/466d8286-5780-40c6-8395-7948c44ac678)

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why

The frontend opened `state.db` with `node:sqlite` for four features. Each one copied a Hermes rule into SQL: which rows are visible, how a compressed conversation chains, what a compaction handoff looks like. A schema change breaks them, and none can work when the gateway is on another machine. Hermes serves all four since hermes-agent #150102.

## What changes

| Feature | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/sessions` list | SQL over `sessions`, `messages`, `state_meta` | `session.list` with `picker: true`, scopes `live` and `stored`, merged |
| Preview | SQL over `messages` | the list row's `preview` and `last_reply`; `session.transcript` with `order: 'latest'`, older pages on scroll |
| Compaction markers | SQL for rows that contain the handoff text | `session.transcript` rows with `row_kind: 'compaction'` |
| Pull-request links | SQL lineage walk, then a read of `pull-requests.json` | plugin RPC `pull_requests.linked`; the event `pull_requests.changed` |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as pane
  participant G as gateway
  participant Y as plugin (Python)
  P->>G: session.list (live), session.list (stored)
  G-->>P: rows with title, preview, last_reply, cwd, workspace
  P->>G: session.transcript (order latest)
  G-->>P: rows, next_cursor
  Note over Y: a subagent calls link_pull_request
  Y-->>P: plugin.hermes-tern.pull_requests.changed
  P->>Y: plugin.hermes-tern.pull_requests.linked
  Y-->>P: linked
```

- **Two scopes.** `live` holds the sessions the gateway serves now, and `stored` holds the ones it can resume. Either one alone misses conversations. Hermes' own TUI also asks for both.
- **Compactions after a resume.** `session.resume` returns the history without compaction rows. The transcript shows first, with no extra call. A background read then pages `session.transcript` (500 rows per call, at most 100 calls) and places each marker.
- **Compactions after a live `/compress`.** The pane reads the newest 100 rows.
- **Links.** `pull_requests.py` answers `pull_requests.linked` for the calling session's conversation. When a link tool changes the list, it sends `pull_requests.changed` to the panes that show the conversation. The pane no longer re-reads the links after each `delegate_task`.
- **Cleanup across the three PRs.** The prompt queue's hold for one named session is deleted (only the private gateway used it), and the tests' fake gateway loses `isCanonical`.

## Behaviour that changes

- The picker lists at most 200 conversations per scope. `session.list` has no cursor. The SQL read took 400.
- The "This folder" tab filters those rows, so it sees only the newest 200 overall.
- First prompt and last reply in the preview are the gateway's shortened text.
- The picker rows have no `repoRoot` field any more, because the gateway has no source for it.
- A session made by `hermes chat -q` does not show. Hermes leaves the `oneshot` source out of every list.

## Verification

- `pytest`: 88 passed. `bun run check`: 941 tests, lint and the three ratchets pass.
- Live, against a real gateway in a headless Tern with the lab's fake model:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/sessions` | the row, its first prompt and last reply, and the preview with its compaction row (screenshot above) |
| Four conversations, one from another folder | all four listed, newest first; "This folder" shows only its own |
| Preview of a long conversation | moving to the end loads older rows |
| Resume from the picker | the transcript loads and a new prompt gets a reply |
| `/compress`, then quit and `hermes tern -c` | the marker shows both times |
| `sublink <url>` (a subagent links a pull request) | the pill `#150102` appears in the parent's pane with no link result in its transcript |
| Quit and resume | the pill is still there |
| `lsof` on the frontend with the picker open | no handle on `state.db` |

![A subagent linked the pull request; the pill came from the plugin's event](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/603ffea0-1fd4-4759-a1a0-ce69524015e8)

## Gap in Hermes

`session.resume` gives no sign that a conversation has compactions, and `session.transcript` cannot filter by row kind. So a resume reads the whole transcript once in the background to place its markers.

</details>

title: refactor(frontend): subagent rows, the hub and the subagent pane read the gateway
body:
The subagent rows, the agents hub and the subagent pane now read the gateway. The frontend no longer opens Hermes' `state.db` or its delegation log files anywhere. A subagent's timeline and pane lose tool output and per-call durations, because the gateway does not serve them.

![The subagent pane beside the chat, read from session.transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42459e35-6cf6-4f5b-b117-fc2abb7cff34)

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why

The frontend learned what a delegated subagent does from two private sources:

- Hermes' delegation log files (`<home>/cache/delegation/live/<id>/task-<n>.log`). The frontend read each running agent's log every second and parsed its line format.
- Hermes' `state.db`. The subagent pane opened it with `node:sqlite`, found the child session by its goal text and read its rows.

Both break when the gateway is on another machine, and both tie the frontend to a log format and a schema. The gateway now publishes `subagent.*` events on the session's stream, and `session.transcript` with `subagent_id` serves a child's stored rows while it runs and after it ends.

## What changes

| Need | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rows of a `delegate_task` card, the agents pill, the hub list | the log file, every second | `subagent.*` events; `subagent.list` once after a resume or a reconnect, and for a nested child |
| One agent's timeline in the hub | the log file | `session.transcript {session_id, subagent_id}`, for the agent shown only |
| The subagent pane | SQL on `state.db`, and the log file | the same `session.transcript` read, from the pane's own connection |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as chat pane
  participant G as gateway
  participant W as subagent pane
  G-->>C: subagent.spawn_requested, start, tool, progress, complete
  Note over C: rows update from the events
  C->>G: session.transcript (subagent_id, order oldest, cursor)
  G-->>C: rows, next_cursor, running
  W->>G: session.transcript (subagent_id, cursor), each second
  G-->>W: rows, next_cursor, running
  Note over W: stops when running is false and a page is empty
```

- **`agents/transcript.ts`** (new). It reads one subagent's transcript page by page. An empty page means caught up, `reset` replaces what it holds, and `running: false` with an empty page ends the poll.
- **One poll per shown agent.** The hub reads only the selected agent. Nothing polls per running agent.
- **Nested children.** Hermes sends only start and end events for a child of a child. Their running tool comes from `subagent.list`, polled while one runs.
- **Deleted.** `agents/liveLog.ts`, `watch/child.ts`, the `subagent.tail` fallback, the log path fields on the row and in the pane's spec, `wire/sqlite.ts` and `hermes/paths.ts`.

## What the user loses

The gateway's display rows leave out tool results (`tui_gateway/session_history.py:339-345`), and a call is stored only when it returns.

| Where | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hub timeline, a tool step | start time, duration, ok or error, result text | the time the step was stored, and the arguments |
| Subagent pane, a tool card | arguments and output | arguments |
| Subagent pane, an ended agent | its exact end (failed, timeout) when a log existed | "done". The card and the hub in the chat still show the exact end |
| Hub timeline, reasoning | the log's thinking lines | reasoning only where a stored row carries it |

## Verification

- `pytest`: 88 passed. `bun run check`: 936 tests, lint and the three ratchets pass.
- A recorded batch of real `subagent.*` events is a test fixture. The rows build from it with no poll.
- Live, against a real gateway in a headless Tern with the lab's fake model:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `delegate slow three things` | three rows, each with its running tool and timer, then done |
| The hub, then T | the timeline fills while the agent runs and stays after it ends |
| The subagent pane | the task and the folded steps show while the agent runs (screenshot above); "Agent 2 has finished" at the end |
| `nested please` | Agent 1.1 shows under Agent 1 with its tool; the pane reads the nested child through the top session |
| A second pane with `hermes tern -c` while agents run | the running rows come back |
| `sublink <url>` | the pull-request pill still appears from the plugin's event |
| `lsof` on the chat and the subagent pane while agents run | no handle on `state.db` or `delegation/live` |

Two cases needed a manual step in the lab. A headless Tern sets no `TERN_PANE`, so the pane was started with the same spec the chat writes. And Hermes ends a session's running children when its last viewer leaves, so the resume case used a second pane.

## Gaps in Hermes

- `session.transcript` with `subagent_id` says `running`, and not how the child ended (`gateway/session_transcript_subagent.py:64-65`).
- The display rows omit tool results and their error flag.
- A nested child's tool calls are not published under its own `subagent_id` (`tools/delegate_tool_progress.py:331-345`).

</details>

title: feat: the session picker reaches every stored conversation
body:
The `/sessions` picker now loads 200 more conversations as you move down, and its search finds titles that are not loaded yet. Before, it stopped at the newest 200. It needs NousResearch/hermes-agent#152645, which is on Hermes `main` now.

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

**Needs NousResearch/hermes-agent#152645, merged as `159f73a162`.** An older Hermes gets the "run `hermes update`" notice when the pane connects. The frontend reads the new fields with its own parser, so `frontend/hermes-src.lock` does not move.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| This folder: 46 of 460 conversations ran in `project-a` | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb231c33-4eb4-44e5-bc66-d409d1b9ca2e) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/385e8ca2-9c07-4cd1-8c98-abe0610ccbe3) |
| The end of the "All folders" list | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f831e2af-7aef-4586-afc1-fbcc28a4de53) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02046447-366b-4618-960e-81880224fab1) |
| Search for `needle`: 5 titles among the 40 oldest | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afddd314-bcf4-47f6-8545-d14e3e8f5349) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18da7d46-68f5-426e-a9fd-52aee9364004) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## The problem

The picker read `session.list` once per scope with `limit: 200`. Hermes had no way to ask for the next rows, so three things failed for a user with more than 200 conversations:

| Where | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "All folders" tab | The list stopped at the 200th newest conversation. |
| The folder tab | It filtered those same 200 rows in the frontend. A folder whose conversations are older showed fewer rows, or none. |
| Search | It ranked only the loaded rows. |

## What changes

Hermes now takes `cursor` and `query` on the stored scope and returns `next_cursor` (capability `session-list-cursor-v1`).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as picker
  participant G as Hermes gateway
  P->>G: session.list {scope: stored, workspace: this folder}
  P->>G: session.list {scope: stored}
  G-->>P: 200 rows, next_cursor
  Note over P: the selection nears the end
  P->>G: session.list {scope: stored, cursor}
  G-->>P: 200 more rows, next_cursor
  Note over P: the user types "needle" and pauses
  P->>G: session.list {scope: stored, query: "needle"}
  G-->>P: the matching rows
```

- **Paging.** The next page loads when the selection is within 10 rows of the end, until the gateway says there are no more. The picker never reads every page in the background.
- **Folder.** The folder tab sends `workspace` to the gateway and pages on its own cursor.
- **Search.** The loaded rows are ranked at once on every field, as before. After a 250 ms pause the picker also asks the gateway, which matches titles and ids in every stored conversation, and adds those rows once each. A reply for text the user has since changed is dropped.
- **Counts.** A tab shows `201+` while more rows may exist, and the exact count when the list is fully loaded.
- **Requirement.** `session-list-cursor-v1` joins the capabilities the pane checks at connect. A Hermes without it gets the existing "run `hermes update`" notice.

In the code, `liveSessions` and `storedPage` in `sessionList.ts` replace `listSessions`. The paging and search state is in `overlays/sessions/listing.ts`.

## What the user should know

- Opening the picker sends four `session.list` calls (two tabs, two scopes) where it sent two.
- The gateway's search covers titles and ids. First prompts, folders and branches are searched only in the loaded rows.
- `201+` is written in the tab's label, because the tab's count slot takes a number only.

## Live verification

A headless Tern, a real Hermes gateway from the #152645 branch, and one store seeded with 460 conversations through Hermes' own session API. Both arms used the same store and gateway.

| Case | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Folder tab | 21 rows | 47 rows: all 46 seeded and the open chat |
| End of "All folders" | stops at `Seeded chat 261`, count 201 | `201+`, then `401+`, then `461`; `Seeded chat 001` is the last row |
| Search `needle` | "No sessions match" | the 5 `needle` rows |
| `session.list` calls for one opening | `live`, `stored` | `live` and `stored` for each tab, then one `stored` call per further page with the cursor |

Run again on Hermes `main` at `ffdc7eeb25`, after #152645 merged, with the same store. The folder tab showed 47 rows. "All folders" ended at `461` with `Seeded chat 001` as the last row. `needle` matched the 5 rows.

Not captured: the "Loading more…" row. A local page arrives before a screenshot can be taken; a unit test covers it.

</details>

title: refactor: the launcher uses Hermes' published functions; adds -w and the quit summary
body:
`hermes tern` now prints Hermes' "Resume this session with" lines on quit, and `hermes tern -w` runs the chat in a fresh worktree. The launcher's hand copies of Hermes' variable allowlist and of the Hermes command are deleted. It needs NousResearch/hermes-agent#152666 and #152675, which are on Hermes `main` now.

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

**Needs NousResearch/hermes-agent#152666 and NousResearch/hermes-agent#152675, merged as `f2d56d6e2a` and `ffdc7eeb25`.** The launcher imports functions that those two PRs publish. On an older Hermes, `hermes tern` prints one line that says to run `hermes update`, and exits.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| Quit after a chat | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0756f3d9-d0b4-410e-a66e-de1ebceece4d) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c81346a-31b0-4727-b21b-e0e894f35848) |
| `hermes tern -w` | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4f7e5f3-7c2b-4e61-ac08-0190dfb6e78e) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d80c158d-8823-4d99-a919-2a068b11a212) |
| Quit a `-w` chat with an uncommitted file | not possible | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/674ce61c-8675-473c-b8d3-44305a142884) |
| After choosing Keep | not possible | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3722fd55-ebf3-47d7-9a2d-78c7ffc4c09c) |
| A Hermes without the functions | not applicable | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/006af1e4-1652-4541-8ad6-86e4798f86f7) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## The problem

`launcher.py` did by hand two things that Hermes does for its own terminal client, and it lacked two features for want of a public API.

| What | Before |
| --- | --- |
| The shell variables sent with a new session | A hand-kept copy of Hermes' name list, prefix list and secret-word list. It had drifted: it dropped names with `SESSION` in them, which Hermes keeps. |
| The command that runs this Hermes | `[sys.executable, "-m", "hermes_cli.main"]` and a `PYTHONPATH` built by hand. A pane keeps it for its whole life and runs it at every reconnect. |
| `hermes tern -w` | Exit 2: "not supported". |
| Quitting | Printed nothing. `hermes chat` prints how to resume. |

## What changes

Deletions first.

- **Deleted:** `CLIENT_ENV_NAMES`, `CLIENT_ENV_PREFIXES`, `SECRET_WORDS`, `client_env()` and the hand-built `hermes_command()`. The launcher sends Hermes' `shell_client_env()` and hands the frontend Hermes' `hermes_command()`.
- **Deleted in the frontend:** the code that carried and applied an `env` part of the command (`connect.ts`, `clipboardImage.ts`, `watch/spec.ts`, `env.ts`). Hermes' command needs no extra environment.
- **One gate for an older Hermes.** The launcher imports the published functions in one place. On `ImportError` it prints one line and exits 1. There is no fallback to the old code.
- **Quit summary.** After a quit (exit code 0 or 130) the launcher calls Hermes' `print_exit_summary(session, command="hermes tern")`.
- **`-w`.** Before the frontend starts, Hermes' `session_worktree.create()` makes the tree and the chat runs in it. After the frontend exits, `finish()` asks about a dirty tree, removes a clean idle one, or keeps it for the session. On a resume, `restore()` brings back a tree that an earlier quit removed.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as you
  participant L as hermes tern (launcher)
  participant H as Hermes functions
  participant F as frontend
  U->>L: hermes tern -w
  L->>H: session_worktree.create()
  H-->>L: the new tree
  L->>F: start in that tree, with HERMES_TERN_SESSION_FILE
  F->>F: writes the shown session's id to the file
  U->>F: /quit
  F-->>L: exit code 0
  L->>H: print_exit_summary(session, command "hermes tern")
  L->>H: session_worktree.finish(tree, session, ask)
```

## Two things beyond the plan

- **`HERMES_TERN_SESSION_FILE`.** The launcher must know which session the pane ended on. The plugin's own pane record is removed on a clean quit, and the gateway's viewer record is cleared. So the launcher passes a temporary file path, the frontend writes the session id there on every session change, and the launcher reads and deletes it after exit. Hermes' own client works the same way.
- **`--resume` takes the short id the summary prints.** `resolve_session` now uses Hermes' `resolve_session_id`, which accepts a unique id prefix. Without it, `hermes tern --resume local-7cee…` from the summary did not find the session's folder, and a removed `-w` tree was not restored.

## Live verification

A headless Tern, a real Hermes gateway built from the three core branches, and the plugin's fake model. Each arm had its own Hermes home.

| Case | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quit after `hello` | no lines | the "Resume this session with" block: `hermes tern --resume <id>`, id, 6 messages, tokens |
| Run the printed resume line | not applicable | the conversation opens with `hello` in it |
| `-w`, clean quit | "not supported", exit 2 | a tree under `.worktrees/`, locked with a `hermes` reason while the chat runs; removed on quit |
| `-w`, quit with an uncommitted file | not applicable | Hermes' keep / archive / discard question; Keep prints "Worktree retained for this session" and the tree stays |
| `-w`, resume after the tree was removed | not applicable | the tree is back at the same path and the chat runs in it |
| `NODE_SESSION_AFFINITY` exported in the shell | not sent with the session | sent, as Hermes' own client sends it |
| A Hermes without the functions | not applicable | one line: run `hermes update`, exit 1, no traceback |

Run again on Hermes `main` at `ffdc7eeb25`, after both core PRs merged. Three cases behaved as in the table: the quit summary, the resume from its printed line, and `-w` with a clean quit (tree made, locked, then removed). The dirty-tree question and the `NODE_SESSION_AFFINITY` case were not run again.

The tests fake the Hermes imports, so green CI here does not show which Hermes is needed.

</details>

title: feat(queue): discard a turn whose outcome is unknown
body:
A queued row with the `unknown` badge now has a `Discard` button. A turn in that state blocks every prompt queued behind it, and the pane had no way to clear it except `/quit`.

![The unknown row with its Discard button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0bc2869-441a-4800-8a63-1b73f199e19a)

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Before and after

Both screenshots show the dock after the gateway was killed while `slow` ran.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/637bb3c0-943f-4e3a-8a81-5fc497d0cfe5) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0bc2869-441a-4800-8a63-1b73f199e19a) |

## The problem

When the Hermes gateway stops hard while a turn runs, the gateway cannot know whether that turn finished. It marks the turn `unknown` and holds the queue behind it until someone says the turn is lost.

Hermes' own clients offer that action. The pane did not:

| Client | Action on an `unknown` turn | Gateway call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hermes TUI | Ctrl+X on the row | `prompt.resolve_unknown` |
| Hermes desktop | `Discard` button | `prompt.resolve_unknown` |
| This pane, before | none | none |

In the pane, the row stayed in the dock with its badge. Each new prompt queued behind it and never ran.

## What changes

- A row with the `unknown` badge shows `Discard`, in the same place and style as `Edit` and `Steer`.
- `Discard` sends `prompt.resolve_unknown` with the session, the admission and its `execution_generation`. The gateway marks the turn as interrupted and starts the next queued prompt.
- If the gateway refuses, the pane shows "Could not discard the turn:" with the gateway's message. The row stays.
- The pane now keeps `execution_generation` from the gateway's pending list. It dropped the field before.
- Rows with no `unknown` badge are unchanged. `Edit` still sends `prompt.cancel`.

There is no shortcut and no confirm step. The desktop app also discards in one click, and the turn's result is already lost.

## Not in this change

- The discarded turn gets no marker in the transcript. Its prompt stays with no answer under it.
- A row this pane sent that turns `unknown` with no reconnect keeps `Edit` and gets no `Discard`. That state did not occur in the live run, where every `unknown` row came back through a reconnect.

## Verification

- The four tests in `appDiscard.test.ts` fail with the five source files at `main` and pass with the change.
- `bun run check` passes: 1002 tests, lint, and the three ratchets. `pytest` passes: 108 passed, 1 skipped.
- Live run against a throwaway Hermes home. The run sent `slow` and three more prompts, then killed the gateway with `kill -9`.
  - The pane restarted the gateway and resumed. The dock showed `slow` with `unknown` and `Discard`, and the three prompts under it.
  - After a click on `Discard`, the queue was empty within 2 seconds and the three prompts each had an answer.
  - The store showed `slow` as `terminal interrupted` and the three prompts as `terminal completed`.
- `Edit` on a normal queued row still took the prompt back into the composer, and the store showed it as `terminal cancelled`.
- The "Before" screenshot is from `main` at `8646bba`. The "After" screenshot is from the code commit `3e558b8`; the commit after it changes only a README line.

</details>

title: fix(frontend): a reply a /steer was sent during reads as one reply
body:
A reply stays whole and in view when you send `/steer` while it streams. Before, the part of the reply that arrived after the steer hid inside the next "Worked for" fold.

![The whole reply in view, then the steer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3351241c-14ba-4537-a9ef-a46e0366d905)

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5 2[1m] Medium</summary>

## Before and after

Both screenshots show the same finished turn. The prompt was `stream the plan with a steer`, and `/steer now do the steps` was sent about 8 seconds into the reply.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35d9ec0e-464a-4e59-894d-98df53fc8c11) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3351241c-14ba-4537-a9ef-a46e0366d905) |

## The problem

`/steer` does not stop the model call. Hermes takes the steer later, and the reply keeps streaming.

The pane adds the steer to the turn at the moment you send it. The rest of the reply then arrived after the steer, as a second text block. When a tool step followed, the fold treated that second block as a work note and hid it.

A redirect is different. It stops the model call, so the text after it is a new reply. #79 handles that case, and it is unchanged.

## How the pane tells the two apart

Hermes stamps each `message.delta` with `turn_id`, `segment` and `offset`. Frames recorded from a live gateway show this:

| Text that arrives after | `turn_id` | `segment` | `offset` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a `/steer`, same model call | same | same | counts on (155, 172, 189) |
| a `/steer`, the next model call | new | 0 | 0 |
| a redirect, the next model call | same | same | counts on |

The stamps separate the two `/steer` rows. They do not separate a redirect from more of the same reply. The pane knows which call it sent, so it does not need the stamps for that.

## What changes

- The transcript store reads the three stamps. A delta with the same `turn_id` and `segment` as the text before a steer, and an `offset` above 0, joins that text.
- The steer line stays after the whole reply. It does not mark the character where you sent it.
- After a redirect the store forgets the reply, so the next text is a new block as before.
- A delta with no stamp starts a new block as before.
- The fold code is unchanged.

## Not in this change

- While the rest of the reply streams above the steer, a "Thinking" row shows under the steer. It goes away at the next step. The view cannot tell a steer from a redirect, and after a redirect that row is correct.
- After a reload, a steer that Hermes took after the reply ended shows as a plain prompt in a new turn. Hermes stores it as an ordinary user message. The reply text is whole both live and after a reload.

## Verification

- The new `/steer` test in `steerMidReply.test.ts` fails with the three source files at `main` and passes with the change. The redirect test in the same file passes on both.
- `bun run check` passes: 1000 tests, lint, and the three ratchets. `pytest` passes: 108 passed, 1 skipped.
- Live run against a throwaway Hermes home, before and after the change:
  - `/steer` during a reply: the whole reply is in view, then the steer, then "Worked for 17s" and the answer.
  - A redirect that cuts a reply: the same on both sides, as #79 left it.
  - `/steer` while a tool runs: the steer sits between two folds, as before.
  - `/quit` and resume: the three turns read as described above.
- The screenshots are from the commit before a rebase onto `main`. The rebase changed no file in this diff.

</details>

title: feat(frontend): report the session's run status to Tern over OSC 7501
body:
A `hermes tern` pane now shows in Tern's inbox and banners when Hermes waits on you or finishes a turn. While Tern is in the background, it also posts a macOS notification. Before, Tern could not tell a busy Hermes pane from one waiting on an approval.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5 5[1m] Medium</summary>

## The problem

Tern reads a status record that programs send to their pane: OSC 7501, the Program Status Protocol (https://mitchellh.com/writing/program-status-osc7501). A program reports `working`, `blocked` (waiting on the user), `done` or `error`. Tern uses the record to:

- mark the pane's icon,
- add an inbox entry and a banner,
- post a system notification while Tern is in the background. This is on by default for "needs you" and off by default for "turn finished".

omp sends this record. `hermes tern` sent only a title (OSC 2) and a folder (OSC 7). An approval sheet could sit open in a background tab with nothing to say so.

## What the user sees after merge

| Moment in the pane | Record sent | What Tern shows |
|---|---|---|
| A turn runs | `state=working` | busy mark on the pane |
| An approval sheet opens | `state=blocked:kind=permission`, message `Approve: <command>` | inbox entry and banner "Waiting for you: Approve: …"; system notification while Tern is in the background |
| A clarify question opens | `state=blocked:kind=question`, message = the question | the same, with the question |
| A sudo, secret or vault prompt opens | `state=blocked:kind=auth`, message = the prompt | the same |
| The turn ends | `state=done` | inbox entry "finished"; system notification only with Tern's turn-finished setting on |
| The turn fails | `state=error`, message = the error | inbox entry with the error |
| The user interrupts the turn | `state=idle` | nothing |
| The user quits | `state=clear` | the record goes away |

A notification takes you to the pane when clicked. You answer in the sheet as before. Tern's notifications have no reply field.

## What changes

`frontend/src/session/programStatus.ts` works out the status from state the pane already keeps:

- the newest open question sheet (`PromptSheets.waiting()`),
- whether a turn or compaction runs (`Activity`),
- how the newest turn in the transcript ended.

`App` calls it after every frame. It writes a record only when the text of the record changes, so a streaming turn sends `working` once.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E[gateway event or key] --> F[frame drawn]
  F --> S[ProgramStatus.sync]
  S -->|record changed| O["OSC 7501 to the pane"]
  O --> T[Tern: icon, inbox, banner, notification]
```

- A question sheet wins over a running turn, because the turn cannot go on without the answer.
- A turn's end counts as `done` or `error` only when this pane saw that turn run. A resumed session's stored last turn reports `idle`, not a stale `done`.
- The message is one printable line, base64, at most 2048 bytes once decoded. Tern drops a whole record whose message holds a control character.
- `surface/osc.ts` gains `reportProgramStatus`, beside the existing OSC 2 and OSC 7 writers.

## What this does not do

- No OSC 9 or OSC 99 text notifications. Tern builds its banners and notifications from the status record, so a second notification for the same moment would show twice.
- No capability probe before writing. The frontend runs only inside Tern, which supports OSC 7501.

## Live verification

- **Real Tern window (0.9.12):** a lab `hermes tern` ran in a background tab against the fake model. With a clarify question open, `tern ctl state` listed the inbox entry `waiting: Which colour?` and marked the tab `waiting`. Answering it added `finished: hermes`.
- **Headless Tern, two clean runs:** the pane's raw output, recorded with `script`, held this sequence: `idle`, `working`, `blocked` (approval), `working`, `done`, `working`, `blocked` (clarify), `working`, `done`, `clear`.
- **Not checked:** a macOS notification posting. The test Mac has notifications turned off for Tern in System Settings, so Tern's log records the post as refused.

</details>

title: fix(render_hints): open HTML pages with tern browser; list gltf fences

<details>

## Why the change

An agent that followed the prompt's HTML advice put the page's source in a file block, and the user never saw the page.

## Special things to note

- The command takes the chat's pane from `$TERN_PANE`, which `tern_env.py` gives every command a Tern session runs. The section only reaches sessions the Tern frontend created, so the variable is always set when the line is read.
- Changing `render_hints.py` needs a gateway restart on each install before new sessions get the new text.

The two lines that changed in `PROMPT` (`render_hints.py`):

```diff

title: feat: the PR pill opens Tern's prs plugin; hermes-tern drops its own PR view
body:
The PR pill (and Alt+P, `/prs`) now opens the linked PRs beside the chat in Tern's `prs` plugin. hermes-tern no longer draws its own PR view or needs a `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

![The prs block beside the chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e534248-563b-47ae-8e97-a2f7504c2242)

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5 5[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why the change

The PR view lived inside the chat: a tray above the composer, then an aside that narrowed the chat. Both drew from hermes-tern's own GitHub client, with a token Hermes had to hold.

Tern's `prs` plugin ([alt-glitch/tern-plugins#1](https://github.com/alt-glitch/tern-plugins/pull/1)) now does that job as a Tern block. It survives restarts, reads GitHub through `gh` with no token, and also lists your own PRs and review requests. hermes-tern keeps only what it alone knows: which PRs this conversation linked. The frontend bundle drops from 1.92 MB to 1.01 MB.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![tray](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2fe83c8-a714-4f44-9b06-95cb2696d7f3) | ![list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e534248-563b-47ae-8e97-a2f7504c2242) |
| ![aside](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f91f36aa-2dd4-4662-aadb-665249416368) | ![page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/302b62d6-e56a-44a5-a880-c36c15e610f6) |

## What stays and what goes

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Stays | `link_pull_request`, `unlink_pull_request`, `list_pull_requests`, the `<pull_request_linking>` prompt section, the `pull_requests.linked` RPC, the `enterprise_hosts` setting (which hosts a link may name), the pill, Alt+P, `/prs`, the sidebar's PR rows |
| Goes | the PR tray, aside and sheet; the GitHub client, its polling, checks, stacks and branch lookup; `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`; `HERMES_TERN_GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTS`; the PR view's CSS; 12 npm packages of the Markdown pipeline it used; the token note in `after-install.md` |

The pill now shows `#22` or `3 PRs`. It no longer colours by checks, because hermes-tern no longer reads them; the block shows them.

## How the handoff works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as hermes tern pane
  participant F as panes/5.prs.json
  participant T as tern CLI
  participant B as prs block
  P->>F: every link change (version 1, prs, cwd)
  P->>T: pill click: tern plugin list --json
  alt prs ready
    P->>F: selected + opened_at (for /prs 22)
    P->>T: tern open panes/5.prs.json
    T->>B: route opens the block right of the pane, or focuses it
    B->>F: re-reads every 3 s
  else not installed
    Note over P: opens the newest PR on GitHub, prints the install command
  end
```

- The file format is version 1 from the plugin's README (§ List files): `title`, `session_id`, `cwd`, `prs: [{url}]`, and on a pick `selected` plus `opened_at`, so picking the same PR twice opens it twice. The pane writes it whole (temp file + rename) and removes it on `/quit`, next to its `panes/<pane>.json`.
- `cwd` lets the block add the PR of the session's branch, which hermes-tern used to look up itself. The block side of that lands in tern-plugins separately.
- `tern open` exits 1 ("cannot open in a file block") when the plugin's route handles the open, although the block shows. `prs/open.ts` ignores its exit code for that reason; the plugin check before it already proved `tern` runs.

## Depends on

[alt-glitch/tern-plugins#3](https://github.com/alt-glitch/tern-plugins/pull/3): the route opens one block per list file and focuses it on later opens, matches `selected` without regard to case, and reopens a page when `opened_at` changes. Without it, every pill click adds another block. Merge that first.

## Live verification

At `d93894f`, in a separate Tern window with its own config and daemon, running this branch's `hermes tern` against the lab's fake model and the `prs` plugin from that tern-plugins branch:

- `pr <url> <url>` linked #151819 and #155575; `panes/5.prs.json` held both URLs in the format above.
- The pill read `2 PRs`. Clicking it opened the block to the right on **This session** with both PRs. A second click focused the same block (`tern ls` still showed one).
- `/prs 155575` opened #155575's page; Esc went back to the list; `/prs 155575` again opened the page again. `/prs 99` printed "No linked pull request #99."
- `/sidebar`, then a row's Open, opened #155575's page in the same block.
- `/quit` removed `5.json` and `5.prs.json`; `hermes tern -c` wrote both again.
- `bun run check` (952 tests, lint, ratchets) and pytest (107 passed) pass. The new test file `prsList.test.ts` covers the file format and the fallback.

Not run live: the fallback without the plugin, because it opens the default browser; the unit test covers it.

</details>

<summary>Claude Opus 5 5[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why the change

T3 Code has a review guide: an agent's tour of a pull request, made of stops with notes, files and questions. Here the chat's own agent writes it, with the model and context it already has, and Tern's `prs` plugin shows it.

The plugin side is [alt-glitch/tern-plugins#6](https://github.com/alt-glitch/tern-plugins/pull/6); merge that first. Without it the tool still stores the guide, and the pane only says how to install the plugin.

## Changes

- `pull_requests.py`, the tool `write_review_guide`:
  - It takes a PR, the head commit the agent read, a Markdown summary and 1 to 20 stops (title, notes, up to 20 files, up to 5 questions). `parse_guide` trims and caps every field and checks `head_sha` is a hash.
  - It stores the guide under the conversation's root in `pull-requests.json`, with the same lock and aliases as the links, and links the PR. Writing again replaces the guide; unlinking the PR drops it.
  - Every link tool's result and the `pull_requests.linked` RPC now carry `guides` beside `linked`.
  - The prompt section tells the agent to read the PR first and not to repeat the guide in its reply.
- `frontend/src/prs/`: `links.ts` reads `{ refs, guides }`, and `linked.ts` keeps both. When `write_review_guide` finishes, the pane opens that PR. `listFile.ts` writes `guides` and `tab` in the format of tern-plugins#6's README. `open.ts` gives guides their own install notice, since GitHub has no guide to open.
- `app/stores.ts`, `app/actions.ts`: `openPrs(pick, tab)`.
- `lab/fake_model.py`: `guide` writes a three-stop guide for NousResearch/hermes-agent#153155.
- `plugin.yaml` `provides_tools` and the README (the tools table, a paragraph and a screenshot).

## Live verification

In the lab, with a separate Tern window and the plugin from tern-plugins#6:

- Typing `guide` made the fake model call `write_review_guide`. The list file got `selected: nousresearch/hermes-agent#153155`, `tab: guide` and the 3-stop guide, with head `1c52ab3`. The block opened beside the chat on the Guide tab (screenshot above).
- `bun run check` passes with 954 tests, including a list-file test for guides and the no-plugin notice. `pytest` passes 108 tests, including one for capping, the errors and unlink dropping the guide.

</details>

title: refactor: the Python half under backend/{launch,gateway,shared}, one launch spec, no module-level ctx
body:
The plugin's Python files move from the repository root into `backend/launch`, `backend/gateway` and `backend/shared`, one folder per process that runs them. `hermes tern` behaves the same; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` maps the new layout.

![The lab chat after `hermes tern -c`, with a subagent's link counted in the pill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b287dd5-45f7-415a-892a-188252341a3e)

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5 5[1m] Medium</summary>

## Why the change

The 11 Python modules sat beside `plugin.yaml`, so nothing said which run in the user's shell (`hermes tern`) and which run inside Hermes' gateway. Three more things made the code harder to follow than it needs to be:

- `pull_requests.py` kept the plugin context in a module global that `register()` set. `charts.py` and `figure_check.py` already close over `ctx` instead.
- The launcher handed the frontend its launch as 11 `HERMES_TERN_*` variables. Two of the names lived in `panes.py`, and a hand-kept list stripped an outer launch's copies.
- Nothing checked which module may import which.

## Changes, one commit each

1. `tests/test_layout.py` fails on `main`: every module must sit under `backend/{launch,gateway,shared}`, and `launch` and `gateway` may import only themselves and `shared`. Planting `from ..launch import panes` in `backend/gateway/viewers.py` turns it red.
2. `git mv` into the three folders, with only imports changed and the launcher's path to `frontend/`. The test passes.
3. `pull_requests.register()` builds two closures over `ctx`:
   - `hosts()` reads the `enterprise_hosts` setting on each call, and `tell(session_id)` sends `pull_requests.changed`. Each handler gets them through `functools.partial`.
   - Core's dispatcher reads the partial's signature, so `session_id` still arrives (checked with core's own `_kwargs_accepted_by`).
   - The tests now reach the tools through `register()` with a fake `ctx`, the path Hermes takes.
4. `launcher.LaunchSpec`, a frozen dataclass, goes to the frontend as JSON in `HERMES_TERN_LAUNCH`:
   - `config/env.ts` reads it with a zod schema. A bad field falls back to its empty value alone, as a bad variable did.
   - `LaunchEnv` keeps its fields, so no consumer changes. `readHermesCommand` is gone: the sidebar's command comes from `readLaunchEnv(env).hermes`.
5. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (the tree, the processes, the import rule, the seams table), and the README follows the move.

`HERMES_TERN_EVENT_LOG` and `HERMES_TERN_WATCH` stay as they are: the lab and a watcher's split set them, not the launcher.

## Verification

- `pytest`: 110 passed, 1 skipped. `bun run check`: 953 tests, typecheck, lint and the strict ratchet pass.
- `hermes plugins validate .` gives the same result as on `main`: the plugin loads, `register()` runs in isolation, and the declared tools match.
- The lab, in a separate Tern window, ran each path this PR touched:
  - `hermes tern -q 'hello from the spec'` sent the prompt from the spec and opened in the launch folder. The frontend's environment held one `HERMES_TERN_*` variable.
  - `pr <url>` linked #153155 and the pill showed it.
  - `/quit` then `hermes tern -c` resumed the conversation with its pill.
  - `sublink <url>` made a subagent link #151819. Its `pull_requests.changed` event, sent through the new `tell` closure, moved the pill to `2 PRs` (screenshot above).

</details>

title: fix(transcript): a notice during a turn stays where it happened; the queued Hermes row reads as one line
body:
A notice shown during a turn now stays at the step where it appeared. Before, the PR plugin install hint sat under every later step until the turn ended. The queued "Background command finished" row reads as one line: "· Hermes picks it up after this turn".

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5 5[1m] Medium</summary>

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (Notice during a turn) | After (Notice during a turn) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bcd5065-6a0c-4fee-bf5a-f10a8cf71503) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40259e56-4ba8-458b-a533-8eaf060b05f1) |

| Before (Queued row) | After (Queued row) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d25b9fb-222f-4bd9-baf6-a885fba8001f) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55d97c46-f85d-4e80-bc48-ca0d4ac23424) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## Why the change

- `Transcript.notice()` pushed an entry after the live turn. A notice from mid-turn therefore sat under the turn's later steps and replies, between the transcript and the working row, until the turn ended. In a 25-minute turn the install hint stayed at the bottom the whole time.
- The dock's queued row drew its note as a second `text` node. A Tern row gives text nodes equal shares of its width, so "starts when this turn ends" started at the middle of the row with a gap before it. The wording also did not say who starts what.

## Changes

- `frontend/src/transcript/store.ts`:
  - `notice()` goes through `event()`. During a turn that is an `event` line inside the turn, the same line background work already used. Between turns it is a notice entry, as before.
  - `#continuedReply` (was `#steeredReply`) joins a reply across events as well as steers. Without it, a line that lands while the reply streams split a word ("ste" / line / "p.").
- `frontend/src/view/queued.tsx`: the row's text and note are one `text` node, the note a muted span after `·`. A long prompt still truncates with an ellipsis, and its Steer and Edit buttons stay in view.
- `frontend/src/turn/queue.ts`: the note says "Hermes picks it up after this turn", or "Hermes picks it up next" when no turn runs.
- Tests: two transcript cases (a notice inside the turn, and a reply that stays whole across one). The tests that read notices only after the turn now read them in the turn. The queued-row helper reads the note from the span. The golden snapshot is updated.

## Verification

- `bun run check`: 955 tests, lint and the three ratchets pass. The new transcript test fails on `main`.
- Live in a headless Tern lab on this branch's bundle, with stubs for `tern` and `open` so the install hint fires and no browser opens:
  - `errands` with the PR pill clicked during step 1: on `main` the hint sits under steps 2 and 3. On this branch it stays after step 1.
  - `background` then `stream`, so the command finishes mid-turn: the queued row reads as one line.
  - A long queued prompt beside it truncates, with Steer and Edit visible.
  - A reply streaming over the hint and the background event stays whole.

</details>

title: fix(transcript): the words an agent writes before asking stay out of the "Worked for" fold
body:
When an agent answers and then asks with clarify, the answer now stays in view after the turn ends. The "Worked for" fold kept only the last text, so a two-line reply after the question hid the answer.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc82fec1-c30a-4c84-a127-c9be624a4dc1)

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5 5[1m] Medium</summary>

## Problem

`foldOf` (`frontend/src/view/workLogModel.ts`) keeps one text per finished turn: the last one. It already makes one exception: the text right before a steer stays, because the user read it before they spoke (`steeredReplies`). A clarify call is the same event, since the agent hands the user the floor, but it had no such exception. So a turn shaped like this one folded the answer:

```
thought → commands → TEXT (the answer) → thought → clarify → TEXT (short reply)
```

The look-back also stopped at thoughts, so a thought between a text and a steer hid that text as well.

## Change

- `steeredReplies` becomes `repliesBeforeUser`. It keeps the agent's last text before a steer **or a clarify call**, and looks back past thoughts as well as empty texts and steers sent one after another. A text with a tool call after it still folds as a note on the way.
- `lab/fake_model.py` gains an `answerask` flow: a command, then a long answer sent together with a clarify call, then a short reply once the question is answered or skipped.

Narration between tool calls folds as before. A sample of the last 30 days of local sessions had 1,969 turns: 98% of the agent texts the fold hides are one-line narration under 200 characters, and this change leaves those alone.

Principles:
- `model-the-domain`: "the user has the floor" is the event, and steer and clarify are two ways it happens. One rule covers both instead of a clarify special case.
- `fix-root-causes`: the fault was the rule for which texts count as replies, not the fold's view. The fix is in that rule, and it takes the steer-plus-thought case with it.

## Before (`main`)

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50399eb0-5d11-4b75-ad4b-a3f09cbcec03)

## Verification

- New case in `workLog.test.ts`: answer, then thought, clarify and short reply folds to `fold:k1,a,k2` / `shown:answer,ask,coda`; a reply with a thought before a steer stays in view. It fails on `main` (1 failed, 27 passed) and passes here.
- `bun run check` in `frontend/`: 88 files, 956 tests, lint and ratchets pass. Python half: 110 passed, 1 skipped.
- Headless lab against the installed core, fake model prompt `answerask`, clarify skipped with Esc:
  - `main`'s CI bundle: `Worked for 17s ›`, then Ask and the short reply. The answer is hidden (before screenshot).
  - This branch, the same session resumed from stored history: the answer shows between the fold and the Ask (after screenshot).
  - This branch, a fresh streamed turn answered with "Delete it": same layout, and the narration "Probing the repo…" stays folded.
  - A `work on it` turn (notes and tool calls in rounds) still folds to `Worked for 13s` plus the final answer.

</details>
